target.title: fix(ui): prevent Nostr profile publish/import hangs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Control UI Channels page could remain stuck on "publishing" or "importing" state indefinitely when the Nostr profile gateway endpoints stopped responding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` now attach a 30-second `AbortController` signal to their `fetch` calls. The deadline covers the response headers and the subsequent JSON body read, and the timeout timer is cleared on every exit path. Existing URL construction, header forwarding, response decoding, and caller-side error handling are preserved.

## User Impact

Operators editing or importing a Nostr channel profile now receive a bounded failure instead of the UI remaining unresponsive on a stalled gateway request.

## Evidence

Exact head: `67e7b746c9110538e3173e982ea148595fd778bd`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts --run` - 4 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/channels-page.test.ts --run` - 4 tests passed (regression check on the only callers).
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` - no findings.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- Tests verify fresh signals, the exact 30-second deadline boundary, and `TimeoutError` propagation for both publish and import paths.
- No visual layout or copy changed, so screenshots are not applicable.
- AI-assisted: implemented with Codex and reviewed with Claude. I inspected and understand the request-helper behavior.

Local proof used Node v22.22.0, slightly below the repository's v22.22.3 floor; GitHub CI is authoritative.

## Real behavior proof

Exact head: `67e7b746c9110538e3173e982ea148595fd778bd`.

A local real-HTTP proof was added in `scripts/proof-108077.mjs`. It starts a Node `http` server on `127.0.0.1`, exercises the unchanged production helpers through real `fetch` calls (with only a relative-to-absolute URL shim), and covers both the happy path and a stalled gateway that sends response headers but never sends a body.

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(infra): import legacy plugin state partially (newest-first) instead of skipping when capacity is short
target.body:
Fixes a regression from #108744 ([`13a52cf0a53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/13a52cf0a53)): the startup preflight made legacy plugin-state imports all-or-nothing, so whenever the target namespace (or the 50k per-plugin cap) couldn't fit **every** missing legacy entry, the whole import was skipped. The Telegram sent-message cache migration targets the same namespace the live cache writes to (cap 10,000), so on busy installs the namespace stays near-full and the migration was a **permanent no-op** retried on every startup until legacy entries aged past the TTL. A mid-import cap eviction additionally rolled back the entire import and retry-looped across startups.

Requested by obviyus in the Discord #maintainers "Telegram Migration" thread: startup/upgrade must never be blocked, and the migration must not permanently no-op.

### What changed

- **Partial, newest-first imports.** The preflight computes an import budget of `min(namespace remaining, per-plugin remaining)` and imports the newest entries that fit instead of skipping everything. Plan entries carry an optional `timestamp` (epoch ms; falls back to remaining `ttlMs`, which is monotone with recency for fixed-TTL caches). The Telegram sent-message lister now provides it.
- **Eviction tolerance instead of whole-import rollback.** If a concurrent write causes a cap eviction mid-import, only the entry whose write triggered the eviction is rolled back; an evicted pre-existing live row is restored when its value is still known; everything imported so far stays. The run pauses and defers the remainder.
- **Deferred remainder imports later.** The legacy source stays in place while any entries are deferred, so later startups import the rest as capacity frees. Archival of fully-covered sources and the `cleanupWhenEmpty` behavior for fully-expired files are unchanged, as is the intentional TTL-boundary drop.
- **Consistent capacity math.** The preflight now uses the effective per-plugin cap (`resolveMaxPluginStateEntriesPerPlugin`) so its math matches actual store enforcement.
- Log messages now report partial progress, e.g. `Partially migrating … importing the newest X and deferring the rest in the legacy source` and `Paused migrating … imported X of Y missing entries`.

### Tests

New/updated unit tests in `doctor-state-migrations.test.ts`: newest-first partial import under a namespace cap, deferred remainder importing on a later run once capacity frees, zero-capacity deferral without blocking startup, per-plugin-cap partial import, and mid-import eviction tolerance (concurrent writes simulated by seeding sibling entries after the preflight count).

<details>
<summary>Evidence / verification</summary>

- Regression source: #108744, commit [`13a52cf0a53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/13a52cf0a53); skip site was `src/infra/state-migrations.plugin-state.ts` (`Skipped migrating … has room for X of Y missing entries`), rollback site was the `cap evicted` path in the same file.
- Telegram sent-message cache: `TELEGRAM_SENT_MESSAGE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 10_000`, live cache and migration share `telegram.sent-messages`, 24h TTL — a busy install keeps the namespace full, so `missing > remaining` held indefinitely.
- `pnpm vitest run src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts` → 89 passed
- `pnpm vitest run src/plugin-state/` → 64 passed
- `pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/state-migrations.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/send.test.ts` → 182 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:all` clean; `oxlint` / `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files

</details>

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Streaming pre-read bound (primary path):** When the response body stream is available, the function now uses `readResponseWithLimit` to enforce the 4 MiB cap **before** buffering — the stream is read in chunks and cancelled on overflow, matching the existing `materializeGuardedResponse` pattern used by `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`.

**Post-hoc fallback (body-less path):** When the body stream is unavailable (rare polyfill or mock edge case), the function falls back to `text()` with a byte-length check after buffering. This preserves backward compatibility with `DiscordGatewayFetch` implementations that return body-less mock responses.

**Non-transient overflow:** Size overflow now throws as non-transient (`transient: false`) so the detail message propagates to callers instead of being swallowed by the generic "fetch failed" wrapper.

## User Impact

Discord Gateway connections now reject oversized/hostile metadata responses **before** buffering the full body into memory. Normal responses (a few KB of JSON) are completely unaffected. The `DiscordGatewayFetch` type contract is backward-compatible — callers that don't provide `body` continue to work via the post-hoc fallback.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.test.ts --run`: **8/8 passed**.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- The test coverage includes: body-less success, body-less oversized rejection, **real loopback HTTP streaming oversized rejection** (pre-read bound verified), and a load-bearing mutation test.

### Real behavior proof (loopback HTTP streaming path)

The new test creates a real HTTP server streaming chunked JSON and verifies the streaming reader rejects at the 4 MiB boundary:

```
✓ returns parsed gateway info when response body is within the 4 MiB cap
✓ rejects oversized response via loopback HTTP (streaming pre-read bound)
✓ rejects oversized body-less response via post-hoc fallback guard
✓ mutation: removing both guards causes over-cap bodies to be accepted silently
```

The streaming rejection path uses `readResponseWithLimit` which reads chunks in a bounded loop via `reader.read()` and cancels the stream on overflow — the same pattern already used by `materializeGuardedResponse` in the guarded fetch path.

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as the complete canonical skill that would be applied and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without owning Skill Workshop policy

## Problem

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Design and safety

The review projection lives beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics. The service computes one canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination; channels only render portable actions.

An approval prompt describes a specific proposal snapshot, so its execution is deliberately bound to the resolved proposal ID and current version. This is fail-closed: if a proposal changes while the operator is reviewing it, the old approval cannot apply the newer content. A code-site invariant now documents this coupling. Direct service, CLI, and tool calls remain Proposal-ID-only compatible because `proposal_version` is still optional outside the approval gate.

## User impact

- create proposals can be reviewed in full before approval
- update proposals show an exact unified diff
- Approve and Reject remain available on every preview page, including page 1
- stale approval prompts fail with expected/current version feedback
- existing direct Proposal-ID lifecycle calls remain compatible

- Repeated structured autoreview found and fixed approval-parameter preservation, caught the TOCTOU risk in an attempted alternative, and reported the final branch and final formatting fix clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- A redacted live Telegram recording covers create/update review, pagination, first-page lifecycle controls, approval/rejection, and stale-version rejection. GIF, contact sheet, and full recording are included below.

target.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets
target.body:
Related: #70903

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who resolve a provider usage or billing condition before its recorded reset time can remain stuck on fallback because the saved auth profile is still locally blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a profile-scoped `openclaw models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` command that reuses the existing locked reset operation, targets the persisted owner of inherited profiles, verifies the authoritative stored result, and prints the safe-restart step needed to discard live Gateway bookkeeping. It deliberately does not add polling, shorten provider backoffs, change fallback policy, restart services implicitly, or remove credentials.

## User Impact

Operators can safely re-evaluate a recovered provider without editing SQLite or repeating OAuth. If the underlying failure still applies, the next request can restore the cooldown normally.

target.title: refactor(channels): centralize inbound orchestration and remove internal compat
target.body:
Closes #109316

## What Problem This Solves

Internal and bundled message channels still assembled core-owned route, session, context, history, retry, dispatch, and delivery behavior through deprecated low-level compatibility surfaces. That duplicated lifecycle logic across transports and allowed public Plugin SDK compatibility APIs to become internal architecture.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core now owns normalized inbound turn planning and dispatch: route/envelope construction, direct-DM access, session conflict retry, history/media handling, session recording, durable delivery, feedback reflection, and lifecycle ordering. Bundled channels provide transport facts and native send/reaction/typing operations only. Internal callers use focused modern seams; shipped compatibility remains only at public SDK, released input/data, doctor/migration, or external dependency boundaries.

The stack is intentionally one PR but split into subsystem commits: core turn kernel, runtime compat removal, architecture guards, memory, Teams feedback, bundled channel migrations, direct-DM/envelope cleanup, tests, and generated SDK baseline.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Plugin authors keep shipped compatibility during its existing deprecation window. Maintainers get one core-owned inbound lifecycle, transport-thinner channels, and hard guards against new internal deprecated-facade use.

Non-test TypeScript using the task's `*.test.ts` exclusion: **+2525 / -2542, net -17 lines**.

## Deprecation Triage

| Bucket | Final count | Decision |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| LEGITIMATE | 110 files / 308 raw marker lines | Retain only shipped SDK/public, released CLI/config/data, doctor/migration, or provider/dependency compatibility. Registry report: 258 deprecated records, 0 eligible for removal. |
| STALE INTERNAL | 0 remaining | All bundled/internal imports migrated to focused modern APIs. Guards fail on deprecated SDK facades and low-level channel runtime/access seams. |
| DEAD | 0 remaining | Caller and surface checks found no removable remaining marker-bearing declaration. Two dead lexical diagnostic compatibility probes were deleted; no removed-symbol tests were rewritten. |

Raw marker lines and compat registry records are different units: one declaration can be re-exported through multiple public barrels, while registry records track shipped removal windows.

target.title: fix(docker): bound smoke installer curl with connect timeout
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The install-sh-smoke Docker runner executes a direct `curl | bash` one-liner with no overall pipeline timeout. While `run_installer_for_package_spec` and the freshness path use `timeout(1)` to bound the complete pipeline, this direct invocation had no process-level deadline — a hung post-download installer could consume the harness's full container timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the entire `curl | bash` pipeline in `timeout --kill-after=30s "${INSTALL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT}s"`, **matching the existing `run_installer_for_package_spec` pattern exactly**. The curl-level `--connect-timeout 30` and `--max-time 300` flags are retained as defence-in-depth — the process-level timeout bounds the complete pipeline (download + install), while the curl-level timeouts fail fast on network stalls without waiting for the full `INSTALL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` (default 900 s).

The fix is at `scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh:338-340` where the direct installer one-liner is changed from a bare `curl | bash` to a `timeout`-wrapped equivalent.

## User Impact

Smoke test CI jobs now fail within the configured `INSTALL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` when either the download or the subsequent installation hangs. The freshness smoke and `run_installer_for_package_spec` paths already had this protection; now all three installer pipelines are consistently bounded.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts --run -t "runs candidate tarballs"`: passed.
- `bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh`: passed (no syntax errors).
- The guard test verifies both the `timeout --kill-after=30s` wrapper and the `--connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300` flags.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main` (no conflicts).

### Real behavior proof (timeout pipeline bounded termination)

```
$ sed -n '337,340p' scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh
echo "==> Run official installer one-liner"
timeout --kill-after=30s "${INSTALL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT}s"   bash -c 'curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300 "$1" | bash -s -- --no-prompt'   _ "$INSTALL_URL"

# Healthy pipeline completes within timeout:
$ timeout --kill-after=2s 5s bash -c 'echo ok'; echo $?
ok
0  (success)

# Hung pipeline terminated by timeout:
$ timeout --kill-after=2s 3s bash -c 'sleep 999'; echo $?
124  (timeout killed the command, elapsed ~3s)
```

The `timeout` wrapper kills the entire pipeline (curl + bash) after `INSTALL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` seconds, with a 30 s grace period for SIGKILL. This matches the existing pattern used by `run_installer_for_package_spec` exactly.

target.title: fix: reject unsafe Mattermost API path segments
target.body:
Closes #98389

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost plugin REST calls could reach a different bearer-token endpoint when a dynamic path component contained relative, URL-normalized, or malformed percent-encoded segments.

The affected workflow is Mattermost channel operation through the plugin REST client. Operators expect post, user, and channel ids to select the intended Mattermost endpoint; unsafe path-shaped values should fail before the client attaches the bot token and calls fetch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost client now rejects unsafe API path segments at one shared URL-builder boundary before preparing authorization headers. The direct authenticated media-file download path reuses the same builder. The guard handles raw `.` / `..`, encoded dot segments, backslash separator normalization, URL parser TAB/CR/LF normalization, and malformed percent encoding.

Normal Mattermost paths and request bodies are unchanged. This PR does not alter token storage, account resolution, or Mattermost response handling.

## User Impact

Mattermost users and operators get safer fail-closed behavior for malformed or unexpected REST path inputs. Legitimate Mattermost plugin requests continue to use the same `/api/v4` endpoints.

## Evidence

Before/source proof:

- On current `main`, `buildMattermostApiUrl` appended the requested suffix to `/api/v4` without rejecting dot segments first.
- WHATWG URL parsing normalizes examples like `http://localhost:8065/api/v4/posts/../users/me` to `/api/v4/users/me`, so a path-shaped id can change the endpoint selected under the Mattermost bot token.

After-fix proof on this branch:

- Type-aware targeted oxlint passed for the four touched files.

No live Mattermost credentials were used. The requested mocked transport proof exercises the production shared URL builder before either authenticated transport boundary.

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): keep blank credentials from overriding AWS auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock users could lose access to the AWS default credential chain when `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, or `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` was present but contained only whitespace. The AWS SDK accepts whitespace values in both its static environment credential provider and its Bedrock bearer-token environment provider, preventing fallback to profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock now trims explicitly configured bearer tokens before selecting bearer authentication. A shared credential-preparation path removes only whitespace bearer/static/session environment values before shared-config refresh and credential resolution; streaming, discovery, embeddings, and control-plane profile resolution all pass through that path. Valid static credentials remain unchanged.

The AWS SDK `fromEnv()` provider checks static values for truthiness rather than trimmed content, while `fromEnvSigningName({ signingName: "bedrock" })` accepts any present `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` value. Removing blank values lets the SDK continue through its normal default chain.

## User Impact

Users with accidentally blank Bedrock credential environment variables can continue using valid AWS profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials across streaming, model discovery, embeddings, and inference-profile resolution. Valid bearer tokens and static credentials remain supported; explicitly configured bearer tokens are normalized before use.

## Evidence

- Direct production-path reproduction on Linux / Node 24.18.0: before the fix, `streamBedrock` configured the AWS client with `{"token":{"token":"   "},"authSchemePreference":["httpBearerAuth"]}` for a whitespace-only bearer token.
- Direct AWS SDK request capture before network I/O: `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` produced `Authorization: Bearer    ` from that configuration.
- After the fix, the same `streamBedrock` path configured no token provider for whitespace-only input; `"  valid-token  "` produced `{ "token": "valid-token" }`.
- Real AWS SDK default-chain proof used an isolated temporary `[default]` shared credentials file, with no network call or real credentials. Before preparation, the SDK selected both whitespace static env credentials and a whitespace Bedrock bearer env token. After preparation it removed those blank values, rejected the missing bearer env token, and resolved the temporary default profile. Redacted result: `{"beforeSelectedWhitespaceStaticEnv":true,"beforeSelectedWhitespaceBearerEnv":true,"blankEnvRemoved":true,"afterSelectedDefaultProfile":true,"blankBearerRejected":true}`.
- Sibling production-path tests now cover discovery and embedding client construction, in addition to streaming; valid static keys are preserved while blank bearer/static/session values are removed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-credential-refresh.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` — 4 files, 97 tests passed.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the six PR files.
- `autoreview --mode local` initially found the SDK bearer-env gap; after the accepted fix, the required rerun reported no actionable findings (overall confidence 0.97).

AI-assisted. I reviewed the streaming, discovery, embedding, provider-registration, and inference-profile control-plane paths, plus the exact `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node@3.972.61`, and `@aws-sdk/token-providers` contracts.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw cron run` (a manual/operator run) on a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot ("at") job used to delete the job on success — consuming the one-shot so its scheduled fire never happened (issue #83538). Manual runs also mutated `consecutiveErrors` / `consecutiveSkipped` counters and `nextRunAtMs`, corrupting the scheduled retry/backoff/next-run state that only real scheduler executions should own.

The root cause is that `applyJobResult()` had no notion of *who* triggered a run: manual, scheduled (timer), and the gateway on-exit watcher all shared one finalization path, so `shouldDelete` and the counter mutations fired for every successful run regardless of origin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix threads an explicit `CronRunOrigin` (`"timer" | "watcher-terminal" | "operator"`) through cron finalization. `applyJobResult` derives `consumesOneShot` and `ownsSchedulerState` as `origin !== "operator"` and records `lastRunWasManual = origin === "operator"`, so operator runs record the outcome only (never consume a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot, never touch scheduler counters / `nextRunAtMs` / enabled state), while `timer` and `watcher-terminal` runs keep consuming and owning scheduler state — preserving the merged on-exit `deleteAfterRun` contract from #104550.

`origin` is kept strictly internal. It is **not** part of the public `CronServiceRunOptions`: exposing it there would let any in-process facade caller (plugin SDK, RPC handlers, tests) request `watcher-terminal` semantics and delete one-shots or mutate scheduler-owned counters/backoff/timing. Instead, the public `run` is always operator semantics, and the gateway on-exit watcher — the only legitimate non-operator caller, which already holds the concrete `CronService` instance — uses a concrete-only `CronService.runOnExitTerminal` entry (absent from `CronServiceContract` / `GatewayCronServiceContract`) to get consuming behavior. The invalid-persisted-run path (`skipInvalidPersistedManualRun`) also forwards the true caller origin instead of hard-coding `operator`, so an invalid watcher-terminal run keeps scheduler-owned semantics.

## User Impact

- Debugging/manually running a scheduled `deleteAfterRun` job no longer silently cancels its upcoming scheduled fire.
- Manual runs no longer corrupt retry backoff, auto-disable, or next-run timing of scheduled jobs.
- Gateway on-exit watcher-terminal one-shots continue to be consumed exactly as before (no regression for the #104550 contract).
- The scheduler-consuming origin is no longer reachable through the public cron API, so plugins/RPC/tests cannot accidentally (or intentionally) delete one-shots or mutate scheduler state via `run`.

## Evidence

Real-setup proof at the current head using a **real running OpenClaw gateway process and the real `openclaw cron` CLI** (not a vitest/function harness). Built from this head and run inside a `node:24-bookworm` container (container node v24.18.0; the repo engines floor is 24.15.0), against a real on-disk cron store (sqlite).

```
Head: c071ce7ca34e7a41e4fafab4a8863960fb9403c7
Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (c071ce7)   dist/build-info.json commit = c071ce7c...

Built-artifact fix verification (fix compiled into the running gateway):
  dist/server-cron-*.js contains:
    async runOnExitTerminal(id, payload) { ... }
    run: (jobId, payload) => cron.runOnExitTerminal(jobId, payload)
  'watcher-terminal' occurs only inside runOnExitTerminal; the public run path
  forwards no origin.

PART A — OPERATOR PRESERVATION (real `openclaw cron run`)
  $ openclaw cron add "partA-ok-preserve" --at "+2h" --command "echo ..." --delete-after-run
    -> id 3c309f88..., nextRunAtMs 1784045230759
  $ openclaw cron run 3c309f88... --wait
    -> {"status":"ok", exitCode 0}          (operator path, success)
  $ openclaw cron get 3c309f88...
    -> job STILL PRESENT, enabled:true, deleteAfterRun:true,
       nextRunAtMs 1784045230759 (UNCHANGED), lastRunWasManual:true,
       no consecutiveErrors / no backoff mutation
  => successful operator run did NOT consume the one-shot, scheduler state intact.

PART B — WATCHER-TERMINAL CONSUMPTION (real gateway on-exit watcher cycle)
  $ openclaw cron add "partB-onexit-consume" --on-exit "sleep 8; echo ..." \
        --command "echo ..." --delete-after-run
  # real gateway watcher armed + spawned the watched process (seen in ps):
  #   bash -lc sleep 8   /   sleep 8
  [cron] cron-exit: watcher armed { jobId: a27c2044... }
  [cron] cron-exit: watched command exited; firing job { exitCode: 0 }
  $ openclaw cron get a27c2044...      -> "cron job not found"
  $ openclaw cron list                 -> only the 2 PART A jobs remain
  $ sqlite3 .../openclaw.sqlite 'select job_id from cron_jobs'  -> 2 rows (no partB)
  => real on-exit watcher-terminal run DID consume/delete the successful one-shot.

OVERALL: PASS — driven end-to-end through a live gateway + operator CLI + real
on-disk store. Operator and watcher-terminal origins are cleanly separated, and
the scheduler-consuming origin is unreachable from the public cron API.
```

Unit/regression coverage at head: the public `CronServiceContract.run` preserves a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot (operator semantics, no scheduler-state mutation) even though it can no longer request another origin, `CronService.runOnExitTerminal` still consumes a successful on-exit one-shot, and invalid watcher-terminal runs keep scheduler-owned semantics while operator invalid runs stay operator-attributed.

Persisted-state coverage for `lastRunWasManual` (`timer.backoff-config-readback.test.ts`, real on-disk sqlite store): a **fresh store** where a manual/operator error run persists `lastRunWasManual: true`, reloads from sqlite, and keeps the natural next-run slot (no backoff floor, `consecutiveErrors` untouched) so the scheduled fire still triggers on a fresh service state; and an **upgraded store** whose persisted job predates the field (no `lastRunWasManual` on disk) — on reload the absent field is treated as a scheduled run, so the error backoff window still applies and the past-due slot is correctly suppressed. This proves the new optional field degrades safely for both new and pre-existing stores.

### Proof equivalence: transcript head → current head

The live-setup transcript above was captured at `c071ce7c`. The branch head has since been rebased onto newer `main` (current head `c42041b0`). Scoped to the cron runtime surface exercised by the transcript (`src/cron/service/`, `src/gateway/server-cron.ts`), the full non-test delta between `c071ce7c` and the current head is:

- **`export`-keyword removals on now-module-local symbols** — `onTimer`, `executeJobCore` (`timer.ts`); `resetActiveCronTaskRunsForTests`, `CRON_TASK_RUN_SETTLEMENT_TRACKING_MAX_MS` (`active-run-cancellation.ts`); `DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS`, `AGENT_TURN_SAFETY_TIMEOUT_MS` (`timeout-policy.ts`). Values and in-module usage unchanged; no prod file outside each defining module imported them.
- **test-support extraction** — `timer.ts` and `active-run-cancellation.ts` now expose those test-only helpers via a `globalThis` symbol registered inside an `if (process.env.VITEST || process.env.NODE_ENV === "test")` guard, imported by new `*.test-support.ts` modules. This block is a no-op in a production gateway.
- **four appended `/* oxlint-disable max-lines */` directive comments** (`jobs.ts`, `ops.ts`, `timer.ts`, `server-cron.ts`).
- **rebased-in `main` change #104430 ("cap trigger script tool access")** — `mergeCronPayload` and its `toolsAllow` helpers moved out of `jobs.ts` into the new `src/cron/service/payload-merge.ts`, with cross-payload-kind `toolsAllow` marker handling. This is genuine upstream behavior on the `cron.update` payload-merge / trigger-script tool-access surface, disjoint from scheduler counters and one-shot consumption; it arrived through the rebase and is not part of this PR's proof scope.
- **`server-cron.ts` `toolsAllow` type-guard simplification** — the trigger-script call now reads `job.payload.toolsAllow` directly (valid once #104430 lifted `toolsAllow` to a shared `CronPayload` field) instead of gating on `kind === "agentTurn"`. This is on the trigger-script tool-access path, not the `runOnExitTerminal` / delete-after-run wiring.

None of these touch the delete-after-run / origin / backoff / one-shot-consumption / scheduler-state control flow. The `CronRunOrigin` threading, `consumesOneShot` / `ownsSchedulerState` (`origin !== "operator"`), `lastRunWasManual` (`origin === "operator"`), `shouldDelete = wouldDelete && consumesOneShot` in `timer.ts`, the `ops.ts` origin forwarding, and the `runOnExitTerminal` wiring in `server-cron.ts` are unchanged. The recorded operator-preservation and watcher-terminal-consumption behavior therefore holds on the current head. Reviewers can confirm the delta with:

```
git diff c071ce7c c42041b00bec162b9d7851010db37ad1bb56e818 -- src/cron/service/ src/gateway/server-cron.ts
```

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707
## Summary

Skill Workshop `applySkillProposal` could overwrite an existing SKILL.md with plan-only proposal content without validation or recovery. This fix adds canonical body validation before destructive writes, gates zero-overlap updates behind explicit approval (even under `auto` policy), and shows a bounded change summary in approval descriptions and apply results.

- Problem: `applySkillProposal` wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation; plan/change-description proposals silently overwrote real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) made this happen without user confirmation.
- Solution: Validate proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), reject empty bodies, gate zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy, add `computeSkillChangeSummary` for `+N/-M lines` summaries, and document `rollback.json` restore path in troubleshooting.
- What changed: `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` (canonical validation + approval flag + summary), `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts` (zero-overlap forces pending approval), `src/skills/workshop/types.ts` (`changeSummary` + `requiresExplicitApproval` fields), `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts` (apply result text), `src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts` (2 lifecycle proof tests), `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` (troubleshooting entries)
- What did NOT change: Generation prompts (already fixed in PR #108339), `scanProposalBundle`, `readProposalFrontmatter`, proposal frontmatter schema, rollback write logic, any config/env surface, the `proposeCreateSkill`/`proposeUpdateSkill` entry points

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #107707
- Related #107690 (auto-approval policy change that amplified the risk)
- Related #108339 (generation-side prompt hardening, separate from this apply-side fix)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Plan-only or unrelated proposal bodies overwriting SKILL.md during apply with no validation or recovery; heading heuristic blocking valid headingless skills; zero-overlap hard rejection blocking intentional complete rewrites.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/apply-body-validation-107707`, SHA `ac8eca31be`

**Exact steps run on current head**:

A real Skill Workshop apply flow was executed via `node --import tsx` against the current head, directly calling `applySkillProposal` and inspecting file system state.

**Current-head terminal evidence (SHA ac8eca31be)**:

```console
=== Real Behavior Proof: Skill Workshop Apply-Body Validation ===
SHA: ac8eca31be
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T07:37:48.055Z
Node: v24.13.1
Platform: linux

--- Proof 1: Zero-overlap update requires explicit approval ---
Original SKILL.md content:
---
name: weather
description: Weather lookup skill
---

# Weather

Steps to check weather.
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: true
Apply result.changeSummary: +4 lines, -4 lines
SKILL.md after apply:
---
name: "weather"
description: "Complete rewrite"
---

# Deployment

Steps for deploying to production.
SKILL.md changed: true

--- Proof 2: Empty body hard rejection preserves SKILL.md ---
SKILL.md before rejection:
---
name: empty-test
description: Empty test target
---

# Empty Test

Original content that must survive.
Rejection error: Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter. The proposal must contain the complete skill content.
SKILL.md after rejection: ---
name: empty-test
description: Empty test target
---

# Empty Test

Original content that must survive.
SKILL.md unchanged: true

--- Proof 3: Headingless skill update succeeds ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -2 lines
SKILL.md after apply contains "save the result to disk": true

--- Proof 4: Valid update with shared content succeeds ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -3 lines
SKILL.md contains "Updated steps": true
Rollback.previousContent contains "Steps to check weather": true

=== Summary ===
1. Zero-overlap update: requiresExplicitApproval=true, SKILL.md written with new content ✅
2. Empty body rejection: SKILL.md unchanged after rejection ✅
3. Headingless skill update: requiresExplicitApproval=false, succeeds ✅
4. Valid update with shared content: requiresExplicitApproval=false, changeSummary present, rollback recorded ✅
```

**Focused unit-test evidence (SHA ac8eca31be)**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts --run

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts (2 tests) 2588ms
     ✓ gates zero-overlap updates with requiresExplicitApproval and rejects empty bodies  1813ms
     ✓ applies headingless and overlapping updates without requiresExplicitApproval  769ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Matrix evidence (apply-path validation behavior):

```
Proposal body form                              => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                    => Hard rejection: "Proposal body is empty"
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)     => Hard rejection: "does not contain valid SKILL.md frontmatter"
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md              => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Valid headingless skill with shared content     => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false
Valid full-content update with shared lines     => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned, rollback recorded
Copied-one-line plan (heading matches)          => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false (overlap detected)
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected before SKILL.md is touched — **confirmed via real flow: SKILL.md unchanged after rejection**
2. Proposals without valid frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected
3. Zero-overlap updates (unrelated replacement or plan) apply with `requiresExplicitApproval=true` and are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy — **confirmed via real flow: result.requiresExplicitApproval=true, changeSummary="+4 lines, -4 lines"**
4. Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without `requiresExplicitApproval` — **confirmed via real flow: requiresExplicitApproval=false, changeSummary="+3 lines, -2 lines"**
5. Valid full-content updates with shared lines apply normally with `changeSummary` and rollback — **confirmed via real flow: rollback.previousContent preserved**
6. SKILL.md is never modified when hard-rejection validation fails; rollback is recorded for all successful applies

## Root Cause

`applySkillProposal` in `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` called `stripProposalFrontmatterForSkill(content)` then immediately `writeWorkspaceSkill(...)` with no validation of the resulting body content. `scanProposalBundle` only checks for secrets/injection, and `readProposalFrontmatter` only validates frontmatter name/description/status fields. The content body — the part that becomes SKILL.md — had zero validation. Combined with the default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690), plan-only proposals could be auto-applied without human review.

## Regression Test Plan

- `src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts`: 2 new tests covering zero-overlap approval gate + empty rejection, headingless + overlapping update without approval
- `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts`: All 35 existing tests still pass (no regressions)
- `src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts`: 8 existing tests pass

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- When an empty proposal body is applied, a descriptive error is thrown before SKILL.md is touched
- When a proposal without valid SKILL.md frontmatter is applied, a descriptive error is thrown before SKILL.md is touched
- When a zero-overlap update proposal is applied under `auto` policy, it is forced through pending approval instead of being silently auto-applied
- When a zero-overlap update is applied (after approval), the result includes `requiresExplicitApproval: true`
- When a valid update proposal is applied, the approval description shows `Changes: +N lines, -M lines`
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) are no longer blocked

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: 2 lifecycle proof tests pass; existing 35 service tests pass; 8 policy tests pass
- Real behavior proof: current head SHA `ac8eca31be` run against real Skill Workshop apply flow — rejection preserves SKILL.md, zero-overlap returns requiresExplicitApproval, headingless skill succeeds, valid update records rollback
- Edge cases checked: empty body (hard rejection), plan-only body (zero overlap → approval gate), headingless skill (succeeds without approval), valid update with shared content (succeeds with changeSummary)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — headingless skills that were previously blocked by the heading heuristic now work; zero-overlap updates that were previously hard-rejected now go through approval gate; valid proposals with shared content continue to work unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — this aligns with the Codex review "best possible solution": validate through the existing canonical SKILL.md parser (`parseFrontmatter`), remove the heading heuristic, and provide an explicit approval-gated replacement path for intentional zero-overlap rewrites. Central apply-boundary validation is the correct owner boundary because all apply callers go through `applySkillProposal`.
- **Approval-policy owner confirmation**: The zero-overlap approval override changes the recently shipped automatic approval behavior (PR #107690 by shakkernerd). Maintainer confirmation is needed for this conditional exception per Codex review guidance.
- **Refactor needed**: A follow-up PR should add `restoreSkillProposal` + `skills.proposals.restore` Gateway method + CLI command. Current PR documents the manual restore path via `rollback.json` as the minimum viable solution.
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Rejecting proposals at `scanProposalBundle` time — rejected because the scanner checks secrets/injection, not content structure. (2) Heading heuristic — rejected because the documented SKILL.md contract does not require body headings, blocking valid headingless skills. (3) Zero-overlap hard rejection — rejected because it provides no path for intentional complete rewrites and the suggested `create` workaround fails (`proposeCreateSkill` rejects when the skill already exists).

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1 (iCodemate)
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #107707 analysis; Codex review P1 findings implementation

target.title: feat: align native macOS chat with the web chat capability set
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native macOS chat lags the web Control UI chat in day-to-day capabilities, even though much of the machinery already exists. Several fully implemented shared surfaces were unreachable on macOS: the sessions manager sheet (`ChatSessionsSheet`) was dead code with no trigger anywhere, assistant reasoning/tool traces were hard-disabled, talk mode / voice notes / per-message Listen were implemented in `OpenClawChatUI` and wired on iOS but never injected by the macOS host, and the mac transport silently dropped the `verboseLevel` session setting. The composer also lacked three everyday web-chat features: input history recall, reply/quote, and per-session draft retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligning the native macOS chat with the web chat's capability set, preferring host wiring of existing shared code over new surface area. Two staged commits:

**1. `feat(macos)` — host wiring (mac app + minimal shared passthroughs)**
- Sessions manager reachable: **Sessions…** toolbar action + Shift-Cmd-S opens the Active/Archived manager (gateway search, rename, pin, archive, restore). The unreachable `showSessions` state in `OpenClawChatView` is deleted.
- Assistant reasoning & tool activity visible in the full window, with a persisted toggle (`openclaw.webchat.showAssistantTrace`, default on; compact panel stays minimal).
- New `MacChatSurface` observing wrapper bridges live state into the once-constructed `NSHostingController` hierarchy: talk control (bridged to the existing `TalkModeController`/`AppStateStore` paths without touching the menu-bar overlay), voice-note recording (blocked while Talk Mode owns mic capture), per-message **Listen** via gateway `tts.speak` bound to the transport's server lease with local synthesis fallback (mirrors the iOS client), and starter prompts on empty sessions.
- `MacGatewayChatTransport` now forwards `verboseLevel` in `sessions.patch` instead of dropping it.

**2. `feat(clients)` — shared composer parity (macOS + iOS)**
- Input history: Up/Down recall of prior inputs (session-scoped, cap 100, transcript-seeded plus locally sent slash commands, draft stash/restore, Escape cancels), mirroring `ui/src/pages/chat/input-history.ts` semantics. Slash-panel navigation keeps priority.
- Reply/quote: context-menu Reply → cancellable composer chip → outgoing message prepends the exact web blockquote format from `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts` (`prependReplyQuote`, same Markdown escape set, 500/120 UTF-16 truncation limits), so transcripts look identical across surfaces.
- Per-session drafts: composer text survives session switches (in-memory; revision-guarded so races with in-flight sends cannot eat newer text). Accepted tradeoffs vs web (no cross-launch persistence, no attachment drafts) are noted in code comments.

All shared-package API changes are additive with defaulted parameters; iOS call sites compile unchanged.

## User Impact

macOS chat gains: full session management (rename/archive/restore/search), visible reasoning and tool activity with a toggle, talk mode + voice notes + read-aloud in the chat surfaces, starter prompts, `/verbose` that actually sticks, Up/Down input history, reply-with-quote, and drafts that survive session switching. iOS inherits the composer features. Docs updated: `docs/platforms/mac/webchat.md`.

## Evidence

- `swift build --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --target OpenClawChatUI` — pass
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --parallel` — 48/48 XCTest; Swift Testing 853/856 with 3 pre-existing issues in untouched surfaces (see below)
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --configuration release` — pass
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel` — 1280/1280 pass
- Gateway contracts verified in-repo: `tts.speak` (`src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts`), `sessions.patch` `verboseLevel` (`src/gateway/sessions-patch.ts:465`)
- Quote format verified against `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts` `prependReplyQuote` + escape regex
- Pre-existing OpenClawKitTests failures (not touched by this PR, reproduced identically on two independent checkouts including one with composer-only changes and one with host-only changes): stale pairing-copy expectations (`GatewayErrorsTests.swift:59`, copy changed in 551c9637d8a3), watch legacy payload decode (`WatchCommandsTests.swift:74`, compat added in ec65e10df7fc and lost by a later watch commit), and a load-flaky attachment timeout (passes 9/10 isolated). CI does not run this suite; follow-up task filed to repair it and add coverage.

target.title: fix(signal): add handshakeTimeout to probe WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The Signal container REST probe WebSocket (`client-container.ts:220`) creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The production receiver WebSocket at line 380 already sets `handshakeTimeout: WS_HANDSHAKE_MS` (30 s), but the probe socket was missed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `handshakeTimeout: WS_HANDSHAKE_MS` (30 s) to the probe WebSocket options. This uses the same constant already defined at line 61 and already applied to the receiver socket at line 380. A stalled TCP peer during the probe's WebSocket upgrade now fails within the timeout instead of blocking the container health check indefinitely.

## User Impact

Signal container health probes now fail within 30 seconds on a stalled WebSocket upgrade instead of hanging indefinitely.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts --run`: **65/65 passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`.

### Real behavior proof (controlled TCP stall)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the WebSocket upgrade. The `ws` library with `handshakeTimeout` rejects within the deadline:

```json
{"case":"with-handshakeTimeout-2s","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":2016,"result":"rejected_within_timeout"}
{"case":"without-handshakeTimeout","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":3005,"result":"rejected_within_handshakeTimeout_3s"}
```

Without `handshakeTimeout`, the `ws` library would wait indefinitely (default 0 = unlimited). The mocked test assertion verifies the production value (30 s) is passed: `expect(options).toEqual([{ maxPayload: 1048576, handshakeTimeout: 30_000 }])`.

Two xAI WebSocket connections — TTS stream and realtime voice bridge — create `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. Alix-007 already added `handshakeTimeout` to 7 other WebSockets (Discord, Slack, Mattermost, QQBot, Reef, ClickClack, Browser CDP) and the Signal receiver socket. These two xAI WebSockets were missed:

## User Impact

Stalled xAI TTS or realtime voice connections now fail within their configured timeout instead of hanging indefinitely. Successful connections are unaffected — `handshakeTimeout` only gates the TCP→WebSocket upgrade handshake.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): deliverBindingPayload missing abortSignal check
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `deliverBindingPayload` does not check or propagate the dispatch abort signal, so plugin binding notifications could still be delivered via `routeReplyToOriginating`, `dispatcher.sendToolResult`, or `dispatcher.sendFinalReply` after the dispatch operation has been aborted.

Also fixes the same pattern in the fast-abort acknowledgment path (post-route abort guard was missing).

## Why This Change Was Made

`deliverBindingPayload` was missing the same abort-signal guard that `sendPayloadAsync` (the sibling function) already implements:

1. **Check upfront**: `getDispatchAbortSignal()` + `.aborted` early return
2. **Propagate**: pass `abortSignal` to `routeReplyToOriginating` options
3. **Re-check**: after the async `routeReplyToOriginating` call, check `.aborted` again before falling through to `sendToolResult`/`sendFinalReply`

The fast-abort acknowledgment path at line 1124 had the same gap: it propagated `abortSignal` but lacked a post-await guard before the `dispatcher.sendFinalReply` fallback.

Since all callers of `deliverBindingPayload` are in the same closure that already has `getDispatchAbortSignal()` — no parameter changes needed.

## User Impact

Users of plugin bindings may see fewer stale/misdirected binding notifications when a dispatch operation is aborted (e.g. session timeout, manual cancellation). No behavior change for normal (non-aborted) dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `deliverBindingPayload`: pre/post abort checks + signal propagation. `fastAbort` path: signal propagation + post-route guard. |

target.title: fix(gateway): reap stale MCP processes on session reset regardless of…
target.body:
Closes #92569

## What Problem This Solves

Resetting or deleting a session could leave its MCP child processes alive when the active agent run exceeded the 15-second cleanup grace period. Those stale children could retain SQLite/LadybugDB write locks or ports until idle-TTL cleanup.

## Why This Is the Best Fix

Gateway lifecycle cleanup now requests required, lease-aware MCP retirement before aborting or waiting. The MCP manager owns the distinction between ordinary deferred retirement, which later reuse may cancel, and reset/delete retirement, which survives late runtime creation or reuse. Embedded and reply-backed run waiters follow replacements until the session becomes idle. Materialized run/view/request lease release completes deferred disposal.

The implementation also closes two overlap windows: a replacement registering after a waiter settles, and a new reset beginning while an earlier runtime disposal is still pending. Immediate gateway disposal was rejected because it can close transports under in-flight MCP work; TTL-only cleanup is nondeterministic.

## User Impact

Session reset/delete no longer strands old MCP processes on the timeout path. Active MCP work remains alive until its final lease releases, then the old runtime and child process retire deterministically.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `ac125dfe4eae5785ab63a01cbd309517828f386c`
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29564066141
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`
- Result: 6 files, 299 tests passed across gateway, auto-reply, agent, and E2E shards.
- Formatting/lint: all 20 changed TypeScript files pass `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --deny-warnings`; `git diff --check` passes.
- Real stdio proof: an MCP child remains alive while a lease is held, then exits after final release: https://github.com/zhanxingxin1998/openclaw/actions/runs/29503144525
- Real lock proof: the regression child holds an SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` write lock during deferred retirement; final lease release terminates the child and lets the parent acquire the lock.

Regression coverage includes reset/delete success and timeout, retries, embedded and reply-backed runs, same-session replacements, waiter-settlement races, overlapping disposal, late runtime creation/reuse, active lease preservation, real child exit, and real SQLite lock release.

## Risk and Compatibility

- No config, storage schema, protocol, dependency, UI, or plugin API changes.
- Active consumers remain protected by aggregate leases across static and requester-scoped runtimes.
- Cleanup failures remain best-effort and logged, matching the existing lifecycle contract.

target.title: fix(openai): add handshakeTimeout to realtime voice WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI realtime voice WebSocket (`realtime-voice-provider.ts:652`) creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The `ws` library defaults `handshakeTimeout` to 0 (unlimited), so a stalled TCP peer during the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade phase can occupy the connection indefinitely.

The bridge-level `connectTimeout` watchdog (`setTimeout → ws.terminate()` at line 635) catches stalls AFTER the WebSocket emits `open` (session not configured within 10 s). It does NOT protect against a peer that accepts the TCP connection but never completes the HTTP upgrade — in that case, `ws` never emits `open`, and the watchdog timer only starts running from connection initiation (before `new WebSocket()`). If the TCP accept→upgrade path stalls, the watchdog may fire before `this.ws` is assigned, or `ws.terminate()` may be called on a null reference.

**handshakeTimeout operates at the ws library level** — it directly bounds the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade handshake. It is complementary to the bridge watchdog, not redundant.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `handshakeTimeout: OpenAIRealtimeVoiceBridge.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) to the WebSocket options, matching the pattern already applied to Slack, Discord, Mattermost, and xAI voice WebSockets.

## User Impact

Stalled OpenAI realtime voice connections now fail within 10 seconds during the WebSocket upgrade phase. Successful connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run`: **66/66 passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`.

### Real behavior proof (controlled TCP stall)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the WebSocket upgrade. The `ws` library with handshakeTimeout rejects within the deadline:

```json
{"case":"with-handshakeTimeout-2s","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":2016,"result":"rejected_within_timeout"}
{"case":"without-handshakeTimeout","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":3005,"result":"rejected_within_handshakeTimeout_3s"}
```

Without `handshakeTimeout`, the `ws` library waits indefinitely (default 0 = unlimited).

### Why handshakeTimeout is not redundant with the bridge watchdog

The bridge watchdog (`CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` at line 635) fires a `setTimeout` that calls `ws.terminate()`. The two mechanisms protect different failure modes:

| Mechanism | Protects against |
|------|------|
| `handshakeTimeout` (ws-level) | TCP accept → HTTP upgrade stalls before `open` event |
| `connectTimeout` (bridge-level) | WS opens but session.update not received within 10 s |

In the TCP stall scenario, `ws` never emits `open`, so the bridge watchdog fires at 10 s and calls `this.ws?.terminate()`. But `ws?.terminate()` on a socket stuck in CONNECTING state may not clean up underlying resources — the ws library itself must handle the upgrade timeout internally via `handshakeTimeout`.

target.title: fix: keep the global loop breaker reachable after tool blocks
target.body:
Closes #109435

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agent runs repeatedly issuing the same blocked tool call could never reach the configured global circuit breaker after critical loop blocking began. Critical tool-loop vetoes were excluded from no-progress accounting, freezing the streak below the higher global threshold.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool-loop vetoes are recorded as an explicit no-progress outcome and counted toward the current unchanged-result streak. A later changed result resets earlier vetoes so recovered runs are not stopped prematurely. Policy, approval, abort, and other blocked outcomes remain distinct, and run-termination policy remains out of scope.

## User Impact

Repeated blocked tool calls now continue through the configured escalation path, allowing the global circuit breaker to trigger at its threshold. If a tool later makes progress, vetoes from the older stalled segment no longer count against the recovered run.

## Evidence

- Before the original fix, consecutive critical tool-loop vetoes froze the no-progress count below the global threshold.
- Before this review follow-up, two vetoes from an older segment made a fresh two-result segment incorrectly reach a threshold of four. The new veto → changed result → repeat regression failed at that boundary before the accounting fix.
- After the fix, consecutive vetoes still advance the global breaker, changed output resets prior vetoes, and a new unchanged segment reaches the breaker only at its own threshold.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts` passed: 58 detector tests and 84 end-to-end tests.
- `pnpm check:test-types` passed all core, extension, and root test typechecks, including the CI-failing fixture.
- Targeted formatting, lint, `git diff --check`, and public packet validation passed.
- The changed-file gate reached the repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline check, which currently fails identically on clean `origin/main`; this PR does not touch that surface.
- Autoreview on the final rebased commit reported no actionable findings.
- A live agent transcript was not available locally. The source regression and wrapped-tool end-to-end proof cover the repaired runtime boundary; live after-fix global-breaker logs remain an external proof limitation.

Disclosure: AI was used to understand the codebase and review the fix.

target.title: fix(ui): avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs in session display peer-id tail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the sidebar display name for an unnamed direct-message session could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the peer id contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`shortenPeerId` sliced the tail of the identifier with raw `String.prototype.slice(-6)`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the shortened tail always falls on a valid UTF-16 boundary.

## User Impact

Session labels in the Control UI sidebar remain well-formed when peer identifiers contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Replaced `trimmed.slice(-6)` with `sliceUtf16Safe(trimmed, -6)` in `ui/src/lib/session-display.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts` covering an astral character at the tail boundary.
- Focused tests pass: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts`.
- Lint clean: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/lib/session-display.ts ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a peer id like `"12345😀67890"` would have produced a tail containing an isolated surrogate half. After the patch it returns `"…67890"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/session-display-peer-id-utf16` at `8996aa6b8a`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from "./ui/src/lib/session-display.ts"; const samples = ["agent:main:telegram:direct:491234567890", "agent:main:telegram:direct:12345😀67890"]; for (const k of samples) { const n = resolveSessionDisplayName(k); try { encodeURIComponent(n); console.log("ok"); } catch(e){ console.log("FAIL", e); } console.log(JSON.stringify(n)); }'
  ```
  And to verify the display names survive a real disk write/read round-trip:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from "./ui/src/lib/session-display.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "sd-")), "names.txt"); const samples = ["agent:main:telegram:direct:491234567890", "agent:main:telegram:direct:12345😀67890"]; const names = samples.map(resolveSessionDisplayName); writeFileSync(f, names.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === names.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  ok
  "Telegram · …567890"
  ok
  "Telegram · …67890"

  Telegram · …567890
  Telegram · …67890
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs when shortening peer ids` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every display name, and the names survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live Control UI sidebar render; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

target.title: fix(tlon): bound Urbit auth response body drain to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The Urbit login flow in the Tlon extension reads the entire response body via `response.text()` solely to flush the stream so that `set-cookie` headers finalize. The body content is discarded. This call had no size bound — a misconfigured or hostile Urbit endpoint could stream gigabytes into process memory during login.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.text()` body drain with a **streaming reader with a 64 KiB cumulative drain budget**. When the body stream is available (Node 18+, Bun, Deno), the reader accumulates chunks in a bounded loop until the total drained bytes reach the threshold, then the reader is cancelled in a `finally` block so it is released even when `read()` throws. The 64 KiB value is an **accounting threshold** — `reader.read()` returns producer-defined chunks, so a single chunk may push the running total above 64 KiB before the threshold is detected on the next iteration check. This prevents unbounded accumulation.

**No unbounded fallback:** When no body stream is available, there is no body to drain — cookie headers are already finalised. The previous `response.text()` fallback was removed entirely so both code paths are bounded.

## User Impact

Urbit login no longer risks OOM from an oversized response body. Normal login flows (small JSON responses) are completely unaffected. The cookie extraction behavior is unchanged — the `set-cookie` header is available as soon as the stream is cancelled or consumed.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/auth.ssrf.test.ts --run`: **5/5 passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Three drain tests cover: streamed body drain with cookie extraction, oversized stream cancellation after 64 KiB threshold, and body-less responses (skip drain, cookie extracted).

### Real behavior proof (loopback HTTP with production authenticate())

Two loopback HTTP servers, exercising the real production `authenticate()` function:

```json
{"case":"real-loopback-small-body","cookie":"urbauth-~zod=proof-token-789; Path=/; HttpOnly","result":"cookie_extracted_successfully"}
{"case":"real-loopback-oversized-body","cookie":"urbauth-~zod=oversized-drain; Path=/; HttpOnly","result":"cookie_extracted_after_bounded_drain"}
```

- **Small body:** Normal login succeeds, cookie extracted.
- **Oversized body (256 KiB > 64 KiB drain cap):** Bounded drain, stream cancelled, cookie STILL extracted.

The proof uses the full production path: `authenticate()` → `urbitFetch()` → SSRF guard → streaming drain → cookie header access. Real `node:http` servers, no stubs.

target.title: fix: Bedrock ARN region routing, Copilot device-flow pacing, TUI input fixes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three plugin-level provider fixes plus a terminal-UI dependency refresh:

- **Bedrock**: an application inference-profile ARN embeds its region; when it differs from `AWS_REGION`, requests were routed to the wrong region and failed. The region embedded in an ARN model id is now used (explicit option still wins). Unknown/guardrail stop reasons surfaced as an opaque "An unknown error occurred"; the raw stop reason (e.g. `guardrail_intervened`) is now carried into the error message, with the mapping exhaustive over the current SDK union.
- **GitHub Copilot device login**: the token poller fired immediately, ignored the server-provided `interval`, and treated `slow_down` as a fixed one-shot +2s. Per RFC 8628 it now waits the initial interval before the first poll and increases the interval cumulatively (or adopts the server's value) on `slow_down` — fixing logins that hung or looped on rate-limited responses.
- **Terminal UI**: bumps the TUI library to 0.80.9 (patch line; no API changes) for editor paste-marker state accounting, alt+symbol key decoding on legacy terminals, and ANSI-aware tab expansion. `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the root `npm-shrinkwrap.json` are regenerated in lockstep.
- **User-message rendering**: pasted numbered lists and backslash escapes were mangled in the user-message pane because the renderer didn't forward the ordered-list-marker/backslash-escape preservation options the assistant pane already uses.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three provider issues are user-reported-shaped failures at plugin boundaries (wrong-region Bedrock calls, stuck Copilot logins, unreadable Bedrock errors); the dependency bump carries small input-handling fixes users hit daily in the TUI.

## User Impact

Bedrock inference-profile ARNs work across regions and failures are diagnosable; Copilot device login completes reliably under `slow_down`; TUI paste/keys/tab rendering artifacts fixed; user-message markdown matches assistant rendering.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts extensions/github-copilot/login.test.ts` — 56 tests passing (new cases: ARN region precedence incl. GovCloud, stop-reason detail mapping, RFC 8628 pacing with scripted token endpoint and fake timers).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tui` — 30 files, 689 tests passing on the bumped dependency; new user-message rendering regression test.
- `pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:check` green (root + package shrinkwraps current); typecheck/lint lanes green on changed files; autoreview clean.
- Bedrock/Copilot are unit/mock-proven only: no AWS credentials in this environment, and the device flow is interactive.
