target.title: fix(chat): preserve PNG attachments in native clients
target.body:
Related: #81608

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw Android chat, Apple chat, and iOS share processing changed every selected image to JPEG before the gateway received it. For PNG inputs this changed the filename and MIME type and discarded transparency.

Scope note: Telegram photo uploads are different. Telegram Bot API exposes compressed photo sizes for Message.photo, so if the Telegram client sends a PNG through the photo picker, OpenClaw receives Telegram-produced JPEG bytes and cannot recover the original PNG. Sending the image as a Telegram file/document preserves the original bytes. This PR fixes the OpenClaw-owned native-client conversions found during the broader audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native attachment processing now re-encodes PNG inputs as bounded PNG output while retaining existing dimension, payload, orientation, and metadata-stripping policies. Large high-entropy Android PNGs continue scaling until they fit instead of being dropped after the JPEG-tuned attempt count. The existing JPEG path remains in place for JPEG and other decoded formats.

This deliberately preserves every PNG, rather than only alpha-bearing PNGs. That keeps the declared format stable without a separate transparency scan while the existing transport caps still bound payload size. Native-app owner confirmation of that product policy is welcome.

## User Impact

PNG attachments from OpenClaw native clients now reach the gateway as image/png with a .png filename and preserved alpha. Large PNGs are downscaled to the existing transport budget instead of silently changing format or disappearing. JPEG, HEIC, WebP, and GIF behavior is unchanged.

## Conversion Audit

- Core inbound storage and gateway staging preserve received PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF bytes when they are already supported and within limits.
- HEIC and HEIF are intentionally converted to JPEG for model/provider compatibility. iMessage performs this before staging, with fallback to the original if conversion fails; model-input and media-understanding paths also normalize HEIC/HEIF before provider execution.
- Oversized or over-dimension opaque images may be resized/re-encoded as JPEG; transparent images prefer PNG and can be flattened to JPEG only when required to meet a hard delivery budget.
- Unsupported inline formats such as BMP and TIFF are converted to PNG for provider compatibility.
- Oversized tool-result images are resized and may become JPEG.
- Camera captures, latest-photo node responses, canvas snapshots, browser screenshots, and other generated frame outputs intentionally use JPEG for bounded transport; they are generated outputs, not preservation of an uploaded file.
- Native WebP, GIF, and HEIC picks continue through the existing JPEG path in this PR because animation/provider/decoder compatibility needs separate policy decisions.

## Evidence

- Android regression coverage writes a PNG file and exercises the real picked-image to PendingAttachment path, asserting image/png, .png naming, PNG magic bytes, and gateway-budget compliance.
- Android high-entropy coverage starts with an 800x800 lossless PNG above the gateway cap, exercises production scaling, and verifies the bounded result remains PNG. The final android-test-play job passed.
- Final-head Android android-ktlint, android-build-play, android-build-wear, and native-i18n jobs passed.
- Apple processor coverage asserts transparent PNG output remains PNG and that planted GPS metadata is removed.
- Apple chat staging coverage asserts the pending attachment retains image/png and the .png filename.
- Apple share processor coverage asserts PNG output stays within the existing payload budget.
- Final-head ios-build passed. The PNG-specific Swift tests passed; the final macos-swift job failed only an unrelated pre-existing ChatStreamReplayTests reconnect timeout, while the two preceding macOS Swift runs passed.
- Final-head build-artifacts failed only its unrelated startup-memory threshold at 425.3 MB versus 425 MB; prior runs passed and this PR changes native files only. Fork authors cannot rerun upstream failed jobs.
- git diff --check passes and the review finding for high-entropy PNG sendability is fixed and resolved.

A physical Android or Apple device was not available in the contributor environment, so maintainer live-client gateway confirmation remains requested.

target.title: fix(ai): bound openai-chatgpt-responses WebSocket with handshakeTimeout and maxPayload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `connectWebSocket` function in `openai-chatgpt-responses` creates a WebSocket connection without any handshake timeout or message size limit. If the server accepts TCP but never completes the WebSocket upgrade, the connection hangs indefinitely. Oversized messages could also cause OOM.

**Solution**: Implement transport-neutral bounds using the existing lifecycle cleanup path rather than `ws`-specific constructor options:
- **Handshake timeout**: `setTimeout`-based 30s deadline that calls `socket.close()` and rejects the promise. Wrapped in try-catch so a throwing `close()` never leaves the promise unsettled. Works across Node, Bun, and browser globals.
- **Message size limit**: Byte-accurate enforcement in `decodeWebSocketData` using `TextEncoder` or raw `ArrayBuffer.byteLength` before materializing the JS string. Correctly bounds multibyte UTF-8 payloads unlike a simple `text.length` check.
- **Regression tests**: Stalled-handshake timeout, oversized message rejection (ASCII and multibyte), and throwing-close resilience.

**What changed**: Two files — source code and tests. ~120 lines net.

**What did NOT change**: No API changes, no `ws`-specific constructor options, no changes to `getWebSocketConstructor()`, `acquireWebSocket()`, or the SSE fallback path.

Fixes #109566

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unbounded WebSocket handshake wait and oversized message OOM risk

**Real environment tested**: Node.js v24.13.1 / Linux / ws library / net module controlled server

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx evidence-collect.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
━━ Test 1: Stalled WebSocket handshake → timeout ━━
  [server] TCP listening on 127.0.0.1:28760
  [server] TCP accepted, holding without upgrade...
  [server] received 377 bytes (WS upgrade request), ignoring
  ✅ connectWebSocket rejected after 5034ms
  ✅ Error: WebSocket connection handshake timed out
  ✅ Timeout accuracy: PASS (expected ~5000ms, got 5034ms)

━━ Test 2: Oversized message → close code 1009 ━━
  [server] WS server listening on 127.0.0.1:28761
  [server] WebSocket upgrade complete
  [client] Sending oversized message (17.0 MiB)
  ✅ Oversized message rejected with CodexProtocolError
  ✅ Error: WebSocket message exceeds maximum size of 16777216 bytes
  ✅ Close code 1009 (Message Too Big) was sent to peer

━━ Test 3: Byte accuracy — multibyte UTF-8 payload ━━
  Character: € (U+20AC) — 3 UTF-8 bytes, 1 UTF-16 code unit
  UTF-16 length (text.length, BEFORE fix): 5941932 chars  (UNDER limit)
  UTF-8  length (TextEncoder, AFTER fix):  17825796 bytes (OVER limit)
  ✅ Byte-accurate check correctly catches multibyte payloads
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All three bounds are verified with real controlled-server evidence. Handshake timeout correctly fires at ~5s with the expected error message. Oversized messages are rejected with close code 1009. Multibyte UTF-8 payloads that would pass a naive `text.length` check are correctly caught by the byte-accurate enforcement.

**What was not tested**: No real OpenAI API call. Evidence uses controlled local TCP/WS servers. SSE fallback path (unchanged) not tested.

---

## Tests and validation

4 regression tests:
1. Stalled handshake timeout — connectWebSocketForTest rejects after deadline
2. Oversized ASCII message — parseWebSocket rejects > 16 MiB payload
3. Multibyte oversized message — non-ASCII payload correctly bounded by byte count
4. Throwing-close resilience — socket.close() throwing during handshake timeout does not prevent promise settlement

## Risk checklist

- [x] Backwards compatible — no API changes
- [x] Transport-neutral — works on Node, Bun, browser globals
- [x] Byte-accurate — correct for multibyte UTF-8 payloads
- [x] Throwing-close guard — promise always settled
- [x] merge-risk: low — ~120 lines net, regression tests + real evidence

## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #109332, attacking the two ~250s serial CI bins that now own main-run wall time, plus a profiled 130s module-evaluation stall:

2. **`core-fast` (268s) and `core-tooling` (265s) ran as single jobs on the full/main plan.** core-fast is import-bound (247s vitest: 181s module evaluation vs 49s tests); core-tooling is test-time bound (173s of spawned-process tests). ## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer-requested bundled follow-up ("do all of it, one larger PR"). After #109332 and the caching waves (#109330/#109425/#109593), these were the measured critical-path items.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve thinking default precedence for listed agents
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 17, 2026, 12:05 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:05 UTC.
Last body edit: July 17, 2026, 2:09 AM (US Eastern Time) / 06:09 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 17, 2026, 1:37 AM (US Eastern Time) / 05:37 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #109276

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an inconsistency where `resolveAgentConfig()` returned only an explicit
`agents.list[].thinkingDefault` value even though its contract says that agent
defaults have already been applied. Callers that inspect the resolved config
could therefore observe `undefined` for a listed agent while the effective
runtime later inherited `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` through another
resolution path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct nullish fallback suggested by the issue is incomplete on its own.
Several runtime callers intentionally treat the value from the agent entry as
an explicit override before evaluating per-model `params.thinking`, the global
default, and provider/model defaults. Returning the merged global value through
those override-sensitive paths would make the global default incorrectly win
over a per-model setting.

This change separates the two contracts:

- `resolveAgentConfig()` now returns the documented merged value.
- `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` returns only the explicit per-agent
  value for precedence-sensitive runtime paths.

The command, reply model-selection, subagent inheritance, gateway session, and
startup-summary paths use the explicit helper where provenance matters.

## User Impact

Consumers of `resolveAgentConfig()` can now rely on a listed agent inheriting
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`. Existing runtime precedence remains intact:

1. session or message override
2. explicit per-agent default
3. per-model `params.thinking`
4. global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`
5. provider/model default

Explicit `off` values remain authoritative because the merge uses nullish, not
truthy, fallback semantics.

## Breaking Changes

None expected. This restores the documented merged-config contract while
preserving the existing runtime precedence order.

## Implementation

- Add `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` at the agent-scope owner boundary.
- Merge `thinkingDefault` in `resolveAgentConfig()` with agent-over-global
  nullish precedence.
- Route precedence-sensitive callers through the explicit override helper.
- Add focused tests for merged inheritance, explicit `off`, and a listed agent
  whose per-model thinking setting must still outrank the global default.

## Code-Path Analysis

- Owner: `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts`
- Public facade: `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Runtime callers: `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`,
  `src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`, `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`,
  `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- Adjacent precedence owner: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`
- Tests: `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`,
  `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`, plus existing command,
  subagent, gateway-session, and startup-summary coverage
- Contract: `src/config/types.agents.ts` and `docs/tools/thinking.md`

## Mainline Comparison

- Official base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@399345e1bb1b472969cf586bd1400536e940a3cc`
- Base fetched/verified: July 17, 2026, 05:37 UTC
- Current main still returned only `entry.thinkingDefault` from the merged
  resolver. Recent same-surface changes did not implement this provenance split.

## Branch/Base Provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@399345e1bb1b472969cf586bd1400536e940a3cc`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/109276-thinking-default-fallback@c58a6f981f64167e33806c0bf936121d13db704b`
- The head branch was created/replayed directly from the official base.
- The fork default branch was not used as the implementation baseline and was
  not modified by this work.

## Dependency/Contract Verification

No external dependency contract changed. The configuration type already states
that `agents.list[].thinkingDefault` overrides
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`, and the thinking documentation already
defines per-model thinking ahead of the global default. The implementation now
preserves both contracts explicitly.

## Labels Considered

- `agents`
- `P2`
- `impact:auth-provider`
- `merge-risk: compatibility` because configuration-default precedence is
  compatibility-sensitive

These are suggestions only; this contribution does not claim maintainer label
authority.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts`
- focused gateway session/startup and subagent tests selected by changed-file CI
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts src/agents/command/model-selection.ts src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts src/gateway/session-utils.ts src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Evidence Source Map

- Successful exact-head downstream CI: [evidence workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29557157953)
  - Tested head: `7592d0e708c7814dc2d1d37bc2487f6a1ff38628`
  - Tested base: `44b79d44ae1353fcd90159605453b43ec190b6e1`
  - Conclusion: success; no failed jobs
  - Passed `check-lint`, agent command, reply/model-selection, subagent, gateway, plugin SDK, Control UI i18n, type/check, and `openclaw/ci-gate` lanes.
- Current head provenance after the successful run:
  - Current head `c58a6f981f64167e33806c0bf936121d13db704b` is a patch-identical rebase onto `399345e1bb1b472969cf586bd1400536e940a3cc`.
  - Stable patch id before and after rebase: `56c224c2908f0adc231d6126d6454fe5926b45a3`.
  - The intervening upstream range did not modify any changed file or the thinking-default contract.
- Baseline comparison: [base workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29555644564)
  - Tested base: `19b5e564d7e363a6249e1704f3363eff81395305`
  - Confirmed the earlier Control UI i18n baseline failure existed without this patch.
- Earlier patch run: [comparison workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29555662547)
  - Confirmed contribution-owned format, lint, type, agent command, model-selection, subagent, and gateway lanes passed; an unrelated timing-sensitive plugin SDK assertion was isolated before the final all-green run.
- Draft-state upstream PR CI: [PR workflow run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29554005118)
  - Skipped as expected while Draft. A current-head upstream run will replace this entry after the PR is marked ready.

## Sanitized Logs

```text
Merged config: listed agent without thinkingDefault -> global value
Explicit override: listed agent thinkingDefault=off -> off
Precedence guard: listed agent without override + per-model thinking + global default -> per-model value
git diff --check -> passed
```

No credentials, hostnames, internal paths, account identifiers, or private
runtime data are included.

## Media Evidence

This is a non-visual configuration-resolution change. The linked Actions run
provides the complete reproducible source-level flow and exact-head result;
there is no UI state or dynamic interaction for a screenshot or recording to
clarify.

## Risk

- Compatibility: callers that intentionally inspect merged config now observe
  the documented global fallback.
- Precedence: mitigated by keeping explicit agent provenance in a dedicated
  helper and by regression coverage for per-model-over-global behavior.
- Performance: one normalized agent-entry lookup replaces an equivalent config
  lookup at the affected callers; no new I/O or runtime catalog loading.
- Security/privacy: no authorization, secret, persistence, or transport changes.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. No schema migration, persisted-data rewrite, config migration,
or irreversible operation is introduced.

## Documentation Updated

No documentation change is required. `docs/tools/thinking.md` and the config
type comments already describe the precedence restored by this implementation.

## Related Issue/PR

- Closes #109276
- Historical same-area fixes: #86689 and #63418
- Adjacent but distinct reports: #80377, #30398, #73529, and #108337

- No live provider call is required to establish this deterministic config and
  precedence behavior.

  this PR.

target.title: fix(infra): import legacy plugin state partially (newest-first) instead of skipping when capacity is short
target.body:
Fixes a regression from #108744 ([`13a52cf0a53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/13a52cf0a53)): the startup preflight made legacy plugin-state imports all-or-nothing, so whenever the target namespace (or the 50k per-plugin cap) couldn't fit **every** missing legacy entry, the whole import was skipped. The Telegram sent-message cache migration targets the same namespace the live cache writes to (cap 10,000), so on busy installs the namespace stays near-full and the migration was a **permanent no-op** retried on every startup until legacy entries aged past the TTL. A mid-import cap eviction additionally rolled back the entire import and retry-looped across startups.

Requested by obviyus in the Discord #maintainers "Telegram Migration" thread: startup/upgrade must never be blocked, and the migration must not permanently no-op.

### What changed

- **Partial, newest-first imports.** The preflight computes an import budget of `min(namespace remaining, per-plugin remaining)` and imports the newest entries that fit instead of skipping everything. Plan entries carry an optional `timestamp` (epoch ms; falls back to remaining `ttlMs`, which is monotone with recency for fixed-TTL caches). The Telegram sent-message lister now provides it.
- **Eviction tolerance instead of whole-import rollback.** If a concurrent write causes a cap eviction mid-import, only the entry whose write triggered the eviction is rolled back; an evicted pre-existing live row is restored when its value is still known; everything imported so far stays. The run pauses and defers the remainder.
- **Deferred remainder imports later.** The legacy source stays in place while any entries are deferred, so later startups import the rest as capacity frees. Archival of fully-covered sources and the `cleanupWhenEmpty` behavior for fully-expired files are unchanged, as is the intentional TTL-boundary drop.
- **Consistent capacity math.** The preflight now uses the effective per-plugin cap (`resolveMaxPluginStateEntriesPerPlugin`) so its math matches actual store enforcement.
- Log messages now report partial progress, e.g. `Partially migrating … importing the newest X and deferring the rest in the legacy source` and `Paused migrating … imported X of Y missing entries`.

### Tests

New/updated unit tests in `doctor-state-migrations.test.ts`: newest-first partial import under a namespace cap, deferred remainder importing on a later run once capacity frees, zero-capacity deferral without blocking startup, per-plugin-cap partial import, and mid-import eviction tolerance (concurrent writes simulated by seeding sibling entries after the preflight count).

<details>
<summary>Evidence / verification</summary>

- Regression source: #108744, commit [`13a52cf0a53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/13a52cf0a53); skip site was `src/infra/state-migrations.plugin-state.ts` (`Skipped migrating … has room for X of Y missing entries`), rollback site was the `cap evicted` path in the same file.
- Telegram sent-message cache: `TELEGRAM_SENT_MESSAGE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 10_000`, live cache and migration share `telegram.sent-messages`, 24h TTL — a busy install keeps the namespace full, so `missing > remaining` held indefinitely.
- `pnpm vitest run src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts` → 89 passed
- `pnpm vitest run src/plugin-state/` → 64 passed
- `pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/state-migrations.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/send.test.ts` → 182 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:all` clean; `oxlint` / `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files

</details>

target.title: feat(bedrock): enable prompt caching for Nova models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #29707. Amazon Nova generation models on Bedrock were still treated as unsupported non-Anthropic models, so OpenClaw forced `cacheRetention: "none"` and never emitted Bedrock `cachePoint` blocks for Nova requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

AWS documents explicit prompt caching support for Amazon Bedrock models, including Nova generation models: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html

This change teaches the shared Bedrock cache policy to recognize Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, Premier, and Nova 2 Lite refs, lets direct Nova requests keep their cache settings, and keeps the existing no-cache fallback for unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models. For Nova, `cacheRetention: "long"` emits the default Bedrock cache point without reusing Claude's `ttl: "1h"` field.

The follow-up commit also preserves configured direct Nova `cacheRetention` values through the normal agent extra-params path, including the explicit `cacheRetention: "none"` opt-out.

## User Impact

Users can enable prompt caching for Bedrock Nova text models without hitting the previous runtime no-cache override. Unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models, such as Mistral, continue to be protected from unsupported cache metadata.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(auto-reply): deliverBindingPayload missing abortSignal check
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `deliverBindingPayload` does not check or propagate the dispatch abort signal, so plugin binding notifications could still be delivered via `routeReplyToOriginating`, `dispatcher.sendToolResult`, or `dispatcher.sendFinalReply` after the dispatch operation has been aborted.

Also fixes the same pattern in the fast-abort acknowledgment path (post-route abort guard was missing).

## Why This Change Was Made

`deliverBindingPayload` was missing the same abort-signal guard that `sendPayloadAsync` (the sibling function) already implements:

1. **Check upfront**: `getDispatchAbortSignal()` + `.aborted` early return
2. **Propagate**: pass `abortSignal` to `routeReplyToOriginating` options
3. **Re-check**: after the async `routeReplyToOriginating` call, check `.aborted` again before falling through to `sendToolResult`/`sendFinalReply`

The fast-abort acknowledgment path at line 1124 had the same gap: it propagated `abortSignal` but lacked a post-await guard before the `dispatcher.sendFinalReply` fallback.

Since all callers of `deliverBindingPayload` are in the same closure that already has `getDispatchAbortSignal()` — no parameter changes needed.

## User Impact

Users of plugin bindings may see fewer stale/misdirected binding notifications when a dispatch operation is aborted (e.g. session timeout, manual cancellation). No behavior change for normal (non-aborted) dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `deliverBindingPayload`: pre/post abort checks + signal propagation. `fastAbort` path: signal propagation + post-route guard. |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.lifecycle-and-bindings.test-utils.ts` | Regression test for mid-route abort race window in plugin binding delivery |
| `extensions/qa-channel/src/inbound.ts` | Optional `abortSignal` parameter on `handleQaInbound`, forwarded into dispatch `replyOptions` |

## Evidence

- **Test suites**: 311/311 dispatch tests pass
- **Type check**: `tsgo:core` — passed
- **Lint**: `oxlint` — passed
- **Format**: `oxfmt` — passed
- **E2E gateway proof (pre-aborted signal through real QA bus + QA channel dispatch)**:
  ```
  ✓ |extension-qa| proof-109109-abort-gateway.test.ts (1 test)
  [E2E] QA bus started: http://127.0.0.1:42989
  [E2E] abortSignal:    aborted = true
  [E2E] runtime:        set (abortSignal wired into replyOptions)
  [E2E] ✅ routeReply NOT called (short-circuited at entry guard)
  [E2E] ✅ Binding reply SUPPRESSED
  ```
- **Mid-route abort race window** (regression test in lifecycle-and-bindings.test-utils.ts):
  ```
  [C] 1. AbortController created (signal.aborted = false)
  [C] 2. routeReply mock invoked — firing abortController.abort()
  [C] 5. Calling dispatchReplyFromConfig with abortSignal...
  [C] 6. Result: {"queuedFinal":false,"counts":{"tool":0,"block":0,"final":0}}
  [C] 8. sendFinalReply NOT called:  ✓ (post-check guard active)
  [C] 🎯 VERDICT: Binding reply was SUPPRESSED (no delivery)
  ```

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707
## Summary

Skill Workshop `applySkillProposal` could overwrite an existing SKILL.md with plan-only proposal content without validation or recovery. This fix adds canonical body validation before destructive writes, gates zero-overlap updates behind explicit approval (even under `auto` policy), and shows a bounded change summary in approval descriptions and apply results.

- Problem: `applySkillProposal` wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation; plan/change-description proposals silently overwrote real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) made this happen without user confirmation.
- Solution: Validate proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), reject empty bodies, gate zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy, add `computeSkillChangeSummary` for `+N/-M lines` summaries, and document `rollback.json` restore path in troubleshooting.
- What changed: `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` (canonical validation + approval flag + summary), `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts` (zero-overlap forces pending approval), `src/skills/workshop/types.ts` (`changeSummary` + `requiresExplicitApproval` fields), `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts` (apply result text), `src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts` (2 lifecycle proof tests), `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` (troubleshooting entries)
- What did NOT change: Generation prompts (already fixed in PR #108339), `scanProposalBundle`, `readProposalFrontmatter`, proposal frontmatter schema, rollback write logic, any config/env surface, the `proposeCreateSkill`/`proposeUpdateSkill` entry points

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #107707
- Related #107690 (auto-approval policy change that amplified the risk)
- Related #108339 (generation-side prompt hardening, separate from this apply-side fix)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Plan-only or unrelated proposal bodies overwriting SKILL.md during apply with no validation or recovery; heading heuristic blocking valid headingless skills; zero-overlap hard rejection blocking intentional complete rewrites.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/apply-body-validation-107707`, SHA `ac8eca31be`

1. Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected before SKILL.md is touched — **confirmed via real flow: SKILL.md unchanged after rejection**

- **Best fix**: Yes — this aligns with the Codex review "best possible solution": validate through the existing canonical SKILL.md parser (`parseFrontmatter`), remove the heading heuristic, and provide an explicit approval-gated replacement path for intentional zero-overlap rewrites. target.title: fix(openai): add handshakeTimeout to realtime voice WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI realtime voice WebSocket (`realtime-voice-provider.ts:652`) creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The `ws` library defaults `handshakeTimeout` to 0 (unlimited), so a stalled TCP peer during the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade phase can occupy the connection indefinitely.

The bridge-level `connectTimeout` watchdog (`setTimeout → ws.terminate()` at line 635) catches stalls AFTER the WebSocket emits `open` (session not configured within 10 s). It does NOT protect against a peer that accepts the TCP connection but never completes the HTTP upgrade — in that case, `ws` never emits `open`, and the watchdog timer only starts running from connection initiation (before `new WebSocket()`). If the TCP accept→upgrade path stalls, the watchdog may fire before `this.ws` is assigned, or `ws.terminate()` may be called on a null reference.

**handshakeTimeout operates at the ws library level** — it directly bounds the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade handshake. It is complementary to the bridge watchdog, not redundant.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `handshakeTimeout: OpenAIRealtimeVoiceBridge.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) to the WebSocket options, matching the pattern already applied to Slack, Discord, Mattermost, and xAI voice WebSockets.

## User Impact

Stalled OpenAI realtime voice connections now fail within 10 seconds during the WebSocket upgrade phase. Successful connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run`: **66/66 passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`.

### Real behavior proof (controlled TCP stall)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the WebSocket upgrade. The `ws` library with handshakeTimeout rejects within the deadline:

```json
{"case":"with-handshakeTimeout-2s","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":2016,"result":"rejected_within_timeout"}
{"case":"without-handshakeTimeout","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsedMs":3005,"result":"rejected_within_handshakeTimeout_3s"}
```

Without `handshakeTimeout`, the `ws` library waits indefinitely (default 0 = unlimited).

### Why handshakeTimeout is not redundant with the bridge watchdog

The bridge watchdog (`CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` at line 635) fires a `setTimeout` that calls `ws.terminate()`. The two mechanisms protect different failure modes:

| Mechanism | Protects against |
|------|------|
| `handshakeTimeout` (ws-level) | TCP accept → HTTP upgrade stalls before `open` event |
| `connectTimeout` (bridge-level) | WS opens but session.update not received within 10 s |

In the TCP stall scenario, `ws` never emits `open`, so the bridge watchdog fires at 10 s and calls `this.ws?.terminate()`. But `ws?.terminate()` on a socket stuck in CONNECTING state may not clean up underlying resources — the ws library itself must handle the upgrade timeout internally via `handshakeTimeout`.

target.title: fix(anthropic): surface HTTP response body in stream error messages

## What Problem This Solves

`streamAnthropic` (in `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts`) builds `output.errorMessage` in its catch block from the bare error message. For an SDK HTTP error this collapses to a status-only string like "529 status code (no body)" and drops the response body that carries the real failure reason, so Anthropic 429/overloaded/5xx failures are hard to diagnose from the surfaced error.

PR #109556 introduced `formatProviderError` and applied it to `google-shared.ts` and `openai-completions.ts` to surface HTTP status + body as "<status>: <body>". The anthropic provider's catch block is the same shape but was missed in that pass. This adopts the helper there so Anthropic matches the other OpenAI-compatible providers; non-HTTP errors keep their existing message via the helper's fallback path.

The CLI (and other consumers) prefer `listGroupsLive` when available, so users who have active WhatsApp group memberships but an empty config-based groups map would see `No groups found.` from `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp`. Fixes #76722 ## Why This Change Was Made This PR adds `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsLive` that fetches groups from the Baileys socket via `groupFetchAllParticipating()`. The function has two code paths: 1. **Process-local controller** (gateway process): uses the existing `getRegisteredWhatsAppConnectionController()` socket — the fast path when a gateway is running. 2. **Standalone socket** (CLI process): when no process-local controller exists (e.g. `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp` as a standalone command), opens a temporary Baileys socket using stored auth credentials from disk, fetches group metadata, then closes the socket. Both paths fall back gracefully to the config-backed `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsFromConfig` on failure. **Revision (c65f61a12):** Explicitly discard the standalone socket close Promise with `void` instead of wrapping in an un-awaited `try/catch`, resolving the `no-floating-promises` lint error flagged by ClawSweeper review and CI. ## User Impact WhatsApp users who have joined groups but haven't manually configured them in `channels.whatsapp.groups` can now see their real group memberships in the directory — from both the gateway process and the standalone CLI. target.title: fix(reef): add timeout and bounded JSON reads to relay transport
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Reef relay transport client (`extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`) calls `fetch` with no timeout. A relay that black-holes the TCP/TLS handshake or stalls before returning headers will hang `ReefInboxConnection.drain()` forever, silently killing the reconnect/backoff loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the same pattern as recent merged fixes that bound network operations (e.g., #106035, #105885, #102865). The change wraps relay requests in `fetchWithTimeout` (15 s) using the existing injectable `fetcher`, so tests can stub stalled responses. Bounded JSON response reads already landed on `main` via #106456 (16 MiB success / 64 KiB error caps through `readProviderJsonResponse`); this PR adds only the missing request timeout on top of them.

## User Impact

- Prevents silent channel death when the Reef relay becomes unresponsive.
- No behavior change for healthy relays; a stall surfaces as a `TimeoutError` at the 15 s deadline and triggers the existing reconnect path.

## Evidence

- New test covers a stalled relay timing out after 15 s; existing main-side tests cover the bounded JSON reads.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts --run` — 10/10 tests passed on the exact head.
- Exact-head controlled-relay proof (real loopback HTTP+WS server, no fetch mocks): healthy pull succeeds; a stalled pre-header request aborts at 15080 ms with `TimeoutError`; a 16 MiB+1 JSON body is rejected with `reef.relay: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`; after relay 500s the inbox backoff loop recovers, drains the backlog, connects the live socket, and receives the pushed entry. Full transcript in the comments.

target.title: fix(infra): gateway pid probe no longer hangs when ps sampling stalls

## What Problem This Solves

`readGatewayProcessArgsSync` (in `src/infra/gateway-processes.ts`) probes `ps` on darwin to read a gateway process's argv **before** signaling it or reporting it as a verified listener PID. The darwin branch already passed a 1000ms timeout, but {BT}spawnSync{BT} defaults `killSignal` to SIGTERM, which an unresponsive or hung `ps` child can ignore. As a result a stalled `ps` probe can keep the gateway process blocked past the configured timeout, hanging gateway signal verification and listener PID discovery.

This is the same class of stall already fixed for the doctor TUI process probe in #109243, applied to the gateway's own pid-verification path.

## Evidence

- The fix adds `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `spawnSync("ps", ...)` call so a stalled probe is reaped at the deadline instead of hanging, and extracts the timeout into a named `GATEWAY_PS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` constant.

```ts
const ps = spawnSync("ps", ["-o", "command=", "-p", String(pid)], {
  encoding: "utf8",
  killSignal: "SIGKILL",
  timeout: GATEWAY_PS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS,
});
```

target.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite startup falls back to the system `mount` command when `/proc/self/mountinfo` is unavailable. That synchronous probe had no deadline, so a stalled `mount` process could block state or plugin database initialization indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback probe now has a one-second hard timeout. If filesystem classification times out, SQLite conservatively uses rollback journaling instead of assuming WAL is safe. Existing behavior for successful mount classification and non-timeout probe failures is preserved.

## User Impact

Database-backed OpenClaw startup no longer waits indefinitely on a wedged mount probe. When the deadline is reached, startup continues with rollback journaling, avoiding both the hang and an unsafe WAL assumption for an unclassified network filesystem.

## Evidence

- Regression-first tests cover the missing timeout and the conservative timeout policy.

target.title: fix(compaction): count CJK text in token estimates
target.body:
Closes #103930

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CJK-heavy sessions retain far more recent conversation than `keepRecentTokens` intends after compaction. The cut-point estimator treated CJK text as four characters per token, so Chinese, Japanese, and Korean content could be retained at roughly three to four times the configured token budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction estimator now uses the repository's existing CJK-aware character accounting for every textual message shape. That helper now lives in `@openclaw/normalization-core`, which both the root runtime and standalone `agent-core` can import without duplicating Unicode-range behavior; the existing root module remains a compatibility re-export.

## User Impact

CJK-heavy conversations now compact to approximately the same retained-token budget as equivalent ASCII conversations. ASCII estimates and image accounting are unchanged.

## Evidence

Before: the unmodified production estimator returned 40 estimated tokens for 160 CJK characters—the same result as 160 ASCII characters—and selected cut point index 1 for four such messages with a 100-token budget.

After, driving the real exported production functions on this branch:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module …
{"cjkTokens":160,"extensionBTokens":160,"cutPoint":3}
```

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): keep spawn pipe streams UTF-8 safe across chunk splits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Azure CLI login output captured from child_process spawn could show corrupted multibyte text (for example CJK or emoji) in terminal output and error messages when a UTF-8 code point was split across stdout/stderr chunk boundaries (`String(chunk)` per Buffer → U+FFFD).

Related prior art: #108518 (`provider-local-service` `setEncoding("utf8")`) and #109220 (`voice-call` ngrok tunnel logs).

## Why This Change Was Made

`azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions` pipes now decode stdout/stderr statefully with `setEncoding("utf8")` before line buffering and output forwarding.

## User Impact

Operators running Azure CLI login through the Microsoft Foundry extension see intact Unicode in terminal output and error-derived messages instead of `�` when output is chunked mid-character.

## Evidence

### Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts` | +8/−4 — add `setEncoding("utf8")` before stdout/stderr data handlers |
| `extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts` | +73/−24 — mock regression test calling `azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions` + real-spawn integration test |
| `scripts/proof-setencoding-utf8.mjs` | +79/−0 — standalone proof script anyone can run to verify before/after behavior |

### Tests

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  95 passed (95)
```

### Proof

**1. Production-function regression test (mock spawn)**

Calls `azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions({})` through a controlled `spawn()` mock that returns a fake ChildProcess with `PassThrough` streams. Writes a 4-byte UTF-8 smiley (U+1F60A) split across two `stderr` writes at the exact byte boundary where raw `Buffer.toString()` would produce U+FFFD, then emits `close(1)`. Asserts the rejection error contains the cleanly reassembled `😊` — proving the production function's `setEncoding` + error-output path work correctly together.

**2. Real-spawn integration test**

Uses `vi.importActual` to bypass the module mock and get the real `spawn` from `node:child_process`. Spawns a real Node.js child (`process.execPath -e ...`) that writes `Buffer.from([0xf0, 0x9f, 0x98, 0x8a])` split across two `process.stdout.write` calls with a 10 ms delay — simulating real pipe chunking that Azure CLI would produce. Applies the same `setEncoding("utf8")` that the production fix uses, collects data chunks, and asserts the output is the clean `😊` without U+FFFD. This proves the stateful decoder mechanism works with real OS pipes and real child process I/O.

**3. Standalone proof script (`scripts/proof-setencoding-utf8.mjs`)**

Anyone can run `node scripts/proof-setencoding-utf8.mjs` to verify the before/after behavior on their own machine. Terminal output:

```
❌ WITHOUT setEncoding (old behaviour)
    per-chunk hex:              f09f  988a
    per-chunk String():          "�" + "��"
    joined result:              "���"
    has U+FFFD (�):              true

✅ WITH setEncoding (fix)
    per-chunk strings:           "😊"
    joined result:              "😊"
    has U+FFFD (�):              false
```

**4. Real spawned `az` end-to-end proof (see PR comment)**

Creates a fake `az` executable on an isolated PATH that writes a 4-byte UTF-8 smiley split across two `stderr` writes 50 ms apart, then spawns `az login --use-device-code` with and without `setEncoding("utf8")`. This exercises the exact same `spawn("az", ["login", "--use-device-code"], ...)` path as the production function, through a real OS pipe buffer. See the PR comment for live terminal output.

Combined proof coverage:

| Layer | What it proves | Method |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| Production function logic | `azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions` handles setEncoding → data → accumulation → close → error correctly | Mock `spawn()` with `PassThrough` streams |
| Real OS pipe decoder | `setEncoding("utf8")` reassembles split bytes on real spawned pipes | Fake `az` on PATH, real `spawn()` with same args as production function |
| Reproducibility | Any operator can verify before/after on their machine | Standalone `scripts/proof-setencoding-utf8.mjs` |

### Non-goals / boundaries

- Does not add Azure CLI binary dependency to tests.
- Does not change `execAz` (uses `execFileSync` with `encoding: "utf-8"`) or `execAzAsync` (uses SDK `runExec` wrapper) — both already handle encoding correctly.

target.title: fix(sandbox): cancel unsuccessful CDP probe responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sandbox browser startup could leave HTTP response streams open when CDP readiness probes received non-success statuses. Each failed `/json/version` probe during the retry loop could retain transport resources until garbage collection while startup still timed out normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForSandboxCdp` now cancels unread response bodies after non-ok probe responses. Successful probes, retry timing, auth headers, and startup timeout behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Sandbox browser auto-start still fails the same way when CDP never becomes ready, but failed probe responses release their connections promptly instead of being left open across retries.

## Evidence

**Real-machine before / premise / after / negative control**

Environment: Linux 6.8.0-134-generic x86_64, Node v24.5.0.

I ran the same production-function harness from an `upstream/main` snapshot and this branch. The harness starts a real localhost `node:http` server, sends a streaming HTTP 503 response through real Node fetch, calls the production `waitForSandboxCdp` loop, and observes the server-side TCP socket 250 ms after the function returns:

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-before
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /srv/projects/openclaw-wt-sandbox-cdp-body-cancel
```

The harness loads the probe loop from `src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts` (mirrored in `/tmp/sandbox-cdp-probe-*.ts` for import isolation). The server never ends its response body, making socket closure a direct observation of consumer cancellation rather than normal body completion.

Negative control / before (`upstream/main` at `e01027dd28a`):

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","cdpReachable":false,"serverObservedSocketClose":false}
```

Premise: non-ok CDP probes returned immediately without consuming or canceling unread error bodies, so the streaming response stayed open after the probe loop moved on.

After (`3b933448b77`):

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","cdpReachable":false,"serverObservedSocketClose":true}
```

The identical `cdpReachable: false` value is the behavioral control: startup semantics are preserved while the real server observes prompt connection release.

Focused validation:

target.title: fix(mattermost): keep finalized preview when a trailing tool-error warning falls back
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #109471.

Fixes an issue where Mattermost preview streaming **deletes a successfully finalized assistant reply** when a later tool-error warning payload reuses the same draft. With partial preview streaming (the default), a turn that completes successfully after a tool failure can emit an ordered `[successful final, isError tool-warning]` sequence. The successful final finalizes the preview post in place; the trailing warning cannot finalize in place, so the shared fallback deletes the now-durable preview post and leaves only the `⚠️` warning visible. The reporter had to ask for status even though the agent had succeeded.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deliverMattermostReplyWithDraftPreview` already records `previewState.finalizedViaPreviewPost = true` in `onPreviewFinalized`, but never read that flag. The adapter's `draft.clear` was wired straight to `draftStream.clear`, which deletes the stored preview post. So once a final had landed in place, any later payload's fallback cleanup (`discardPending` → normal send → `clear` in the shared `deliverFinalizableLivePreview`) deleted the finalized answer.

The fix wraps the adapter's `draft.clear` so that when `previewState.finalizedViaPreviewPost` is already `true`, the clear is a no-op. The trailing warning is still delivered as a separate, durable post via `deliverNormally`; only the destructive deletion of the finalized preview is suppressed. `discardPending` is untouched (it stops the stream but does not delete).

The change is confined to the Mattermost plugin (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-draft-delivery.ts`). The shared core adapter `src/channels/message/live.ts` — which has sibling channel users — is intentionally not modified.

## User Impact

Mattermost users keep the successful assistant answer and receive any later tool-error warning as a separate message, instead of having the answer replaced/removed by the warning. The skill remains usable by the gateway/model throughout; this corrects misleading UI/delivery state, not a functional skill failure.

## Evidence

### Real-path behavior proof (wire-level)
A new real-path test in `delivery-trace.test.ts` drives the **real** draft stream + **real** delivery wiring (`createMattermostDraftStream` + `deliverMattermostReplyWithDraftPreview` + `deliverMattermostReplyPayload`); only the Mattermost HTTP endpoint is a recording client. It runs the reported ordered `[successful final, isError tool-warning]` sequence and asserts the resulting REST calls. Observed wire traces from the harness:

```text
# WITH the fix (current PR):
POST /posts            # streaming preview created (post-1)
PUT  /posts/post-1     # successful final finalizes the answer in place
POST /posts            # trailing tool-error warning delivered as a separate post
# (no DELETE — the finalized answer post is preserved)

# WITH the guard reverted (reproduces the bug):
POST /posts
PUT  /posts/post-1
POST /posts
DELETE /posts/post-1   # finalized answer deleted — the reported symptom
```

The test fails on the reverted code (`expected [ 'DELETE /posts/post-1' ] to deeply equal []`) and passes with the fix. This is an API trace produced by real production code (the recording client stands in for the Mattermost HTTP endpoint, as in the existing delivery-trace goldens); it is not a live Mattermost server run.

### Tests
- **TDD unit test** (`monitor.test.ts`): fails without the fix (`expected vi.fn() to not be called... been called 1 times`), passes with it.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/delivery-trace.test.ts` — 57/57 pass (includes the golden delivery traces).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost` — 598 pass; 3 failures (`model-picker`, `thread-participation` store, `setup` wizard) reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (verified by stashing this change), so they are pre-existing/environmental and unrelated.
- `oxfmt --check`, targeted `oxlint`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Autoreview (claude engine, `claude-fable-5`) on the full branch: clean — "patch is correct" (**1.0 confidence**), no accepted/actionable findings.

### Proof gap (CI-gated)
This contribution envelope runs Node 22.22.0, below the repo's `>=22.22.3` requirement, so the root `preinstall` gate blocked `pnpm install` completion and the local `check-changed`/Testbox fan-out. Vitest ran on source via the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/* → src` alias (no build needed). A **live Mattermost server run** (real bot account + gateway round-trip) was not produced in this envelope; GitHub CI provides the full typecheck/lint/build/release lane, and a maintainer may still request a live transcript before merge.

AI-assisted implementation and review; the contributor reviewed the diff and evidence before publishing. This is an independent alternative to #109555 for the same issue — different mechanism (guard `clear` vs. omit the draft handle), same owner boundary — provided for maintainers to choose.

target.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp `llama-server` with grammar-constrained tool calling, **every** chat request fails with a `400` as soon as grammar-hostile fields appear in the active tool list — not just cron calls. [#108580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108580) documents three distinct GBNF blockers (each masking the next):

1. **Unanchored pattern** — `declarationKey` used `pattern: "\\S"` → `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`.
2. **PCRE shorthand** — even anchored `^\\S+$` or `^[\\s\\S]*\\S[\\s\\S]*$` fails; llama.cpp rejects `\\S`/`\\s` unknown escapes.
3. **Oversized maxLength** — `trigger.script` `maxLength: 65536` exceeds the ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Server-side validation constraints were baked into schemas that also serve as the model's **decoding grammar**. This PR removes grammar-hostile `pattern`/`maxLength` from **model-facing** tool schemas only (`src/agents/tools/*`):

| Field | Removed from model schema | Still enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `cron` `job.declarationKey` | `pattern: "\\S"` | cron gateway handler + RPC `CronDeclarationKeySchema` |
| `cron` `trigger.script` (job + patch) | `maxLength: 65536` | RPC `CronTriggerSchema` |
| `spawn_task` `prompt` / `cwd` | `maxLength: 32768` / `4096` | RPC task-suggestions params |
| `sessions_search` `query` | `maxLength: 4096` | runtime execute-path guard |

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` is **intentionally unchanged** (RPC contract only; never compiled into model grammar).

## User Impact

Users on llama.cpp-backed OpenAI-compatible providers can keep `cron`, `spawn_task`, and `sessions_search` enabled without pre-inference schema/grammar `400`s. Server-side validation unchanged for normal inputs.

## Evidence

### Regression guard
`src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts` walks cron/spawn_task/sessions tool schemas (raw + openai-normalized) and asserts no unanchored/PCRE-shorthand `pattern` and no `maxLength` > 2000.

### Focused tests (local, head `8bad86f1dd4`)
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts
```
15 passed; `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` current.

### Live llama.cpp before/after proof (local)
Environment: `llama-server` b9960 (Homebrew), `ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b-GGUF:Q4_K_M`, `--jinja`, OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the real OpenClaw cron tool schema (`normalizeToolParameterSchema`, `modelProvider: openai`).

```
llama.cpp endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
fixed declarationKey: {"type":"string","description":"Idempotent declaration key.","minLength":1,"maxLength":200}
fixed trigger.script: {"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"Trigger script source (max 65536 chars)."}

=== BROKEN: unanchored declarationKey pattern \\S (shipped 2026.7.1) ===
HTTP 400
error_preview: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Unable to generate parser for this template. Automatic parser generation failed: JSON schema conversion failed:\nPattern must start with '^' and end with '$'","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

=== BROKEN: trigger.script maxLength 65536 (#108580 constraint 3) ===
HTTP 400
error_preview: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

=== FIXED: current PR model-facing cron schema ===
HTTP 200
inference_ok: true
reply_preview: Hello! How can I help you today?
```

**Interpretation:** shipped schema fails with the exact errors reported in #108473/#108580; this PR's model-facing schema compiles and reaches inference (HTTP 200).

### vs #108671
Same model-facing GBNF strategy as @wsyjh8's #108671. This PR adds live before/after `llama-server` proof and is rebased on current `main` with green CI (including `check-lint` after #108857 discord test split landed on main).

target.title: fix: isolate coding-agent Codex CLI with dedicated CODEX_HOME
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who run the bundled `coding-agent` skill with Codex CLI against the ambient Codex home (`$CODEX_HOME` / `~/.codex`) while OpenClaw holds ChatGPT OAuth for the same account would hit persistent OpenClaw OAuth refresh failures (`refresh_token_reused` / login-expired guidance).

## Why This Change Was Made

The skill’s documented Codex launch form previously ran ambient `codex exec`, which can share and rotate ChatGPT refresh tokens with OpenClaw’s OAuth profile. This change makes a dedicated worker `CODEX_HOME` mandatory for Codex workers: one-time `codex login` into that home, `codex login status` preflight, and command-scoped `CODEX_HOME` only on Codex worker commands so OpenClaw remains the canonical OAuth owner. No runtime auth APIs, provider plugins, or config knobs change.

Fix quality: compatibility — docs/skill guidance only, no config/API break; performance — none (static docs); usability — explicit setup + preflight instead of silent collision; security — keeps OpenClaw OAuth ownership boundary and avoids sharing refresh tokens with external workers.

## User Impact

Operators who enable `coding-agent` and use Codex CLI get clear isolation instructions. Codex workers use `~/.codex-coding-agent` (or another dedicated home) so OpenClaw ChatGPT OAuth stays usable after worker launches. Claude Code and OpenCode launch forms are unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass). Docs/skill-only change.

```text
$ git diff --check
# clean

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md docs/concepts/oauth.md
All matched files use the correct format.

$ # ambient launch form removed
$ grep -nE 'command:"codex exec' skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md
# no matches (PASS)

$ # isolation contract present
$ grep -n 'CODEX_HOME=\|codex-coding-agent\|codex login status\|refresh_token_reused' skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md
# hard rule + isolation section + scoped launch forms (PASS)

$ grep -n 'coding-agent\|CODEX_HOME' docs/concepts/oauth.md
# oauth token-sink note points at coding-agent ambient collision (PASS)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Bundled coding-agent Codex launch must not document or encourage ambient `codex exec` against `~/.codex` / ambient `$CODEX_HOME` when OpenClaw ChatGPT OAuth is in use; workers must use a dedicated, command-scoped `CODEX_HOME`.
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at `main` + this patch (`fix/109704-coding-agent-codex-home`), source inspection of `skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md` and `docs/concepts/oauth.md`.
- Current-main contrast: On `origin/main`, both Codex launch forms are ambient:
  ```text
  command:"codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
  ```
  with no dedicated worker home, no `codex login` isolation, and no preflight. That matches the reported collision path.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `git show origin/main:skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md | grep -n 'codex exec'`
  2. `grep -nE 'command:"codex exec' skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md` (expect empty)
  3. `grep -n 'CODEX_HOME=\|codex-coding-agent\|codex login status' skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md`
  4. `grep -n 'coding-agent' docs/concepts/oauth.md`
- Evidence after fix: Launch forms require `CODEX_HOME="$HOME/.codex-coding-agent" codex exec …`; hard rules + “Codex credential isolation” section require one-time worker `codex login`, `codex login status` preflight, and forbid falling back to ambient `~/.codex`. OAuth docs mention the coding-agent ambient collision class.
- Control check: Only Codex launch paths changed; Claude Code and OpenCode forms still omit `CODEX_HOME`. No OpenClaw runtime auth modules modified.
- Observed result after fix: Ambient `codex exec` guidance is gone; every documented Codex worker path is command-scoped to a dedicated worker home with explicit login/preflight.
- What was not tested: Live dual ChatGPT OAuth login + real `codex exec` worker + OpenClaw model refresh end-to-end (requires interactive account login). Source-level contract proof matches ClawSweeper `source-repro` acceptance for this skill/docs repair.

Fixes #109704

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who run Perplexity web search with `date_after` or `date_before` would not get the requested published-date filtering on the native Perplexity Search API path.

OpenClaw exposes `date_after` and `date_before` as user-facing web search parameters. Those values are validated and converted from `YYYY-MM-DD` into Perplexity's expected `M/D/YYYY` date format, but the final native Search API request used the wrong JSON field names:

- `search_after_date`
- `search_before_date`

Perplexity's Search API documents the fields as:

- `search_after_date_filter`
- `search_before_date_filter`

Example before this change:

```json
{
  "query": "OpenClaw releases",
  "date_after": "2024-01-01",
  "date_before": "2024-06-30"
}
```

OpenClaw correctly validated the date range and converted it to Perplexity-style dates, but the outbound request body used non-contract field names:

```json
{
  "query": "OpenClaw releases",
  "max_results": 5,
  "search_after_date": "1/1/2024",
  "search_before_date": "6/30/2024"
}
```

That means users asking for a bounded Perplexity search could receive an API validation error or unbounded results instead of results constrained to the requested publication window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Perplexity native Search API request body now uses the documented date-filter fields while preserving OpenClaw's existing user-facing `date_after` / `date_before` parameter names.

The request body construction is kept local to the Perplexity provider runtime and reused by the existing Search API dispatch path. This keeps the fix scoped to the provider-owned API mapping and does not add configuration, SDK surface, new provider behavior, or any OpenRouter/chat-completions compatibility changes.

The OpenRouter and Perplexity chat-completions path is intentionally unchanged. OpenClaw already rejects Search API-only filters on that path with explicit user-facing errors.

## User Impact

Users can now rely on Perplexity native Search API date filters to constrain results by publication date.

This matters for workflows such as:

- searching only releases or announcements published in a specific window
- excluding stale search results when investigating recent behavior
- comparing search results before and after a product or dependency change
- running date-bounded research prompts through OpenClaw's web search tool

The visible user-facing parameters remain the same:

```json
{
  "date_after": "2024-01-01",
  "date_before": "2024-06-30"
}
```

Only the provider-facing Perplexity request body changes.

## Evidence

Source and contract evidence:

- OpenClaw's Perplexity provider advertises `date_after` and `date_before` for the native Search API path: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.ts`
- The runtime validates `date_after` / `date_before`, rejects invalid ranges, and converts ISO dates through `isoToPerplexityDate`: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`
- Before this change, the Perplexity native Search API body used `search_after_date` and `search_before_date`: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`
- Perplexity's official Search API reference documents `search_after_date_filter` and `search_before_date_filter`: https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/search-post

Focused regression test added:

- `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts` verifies the native Search API request body maps converted dates to:
  - `search_after_date_filter`
  - `search_before_date_filter`
- The test also proves the existing user-facing date format conversion remains compatible with the provider-facing `M/D/YYYY` values.

Validation run:

```bash
OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts
```

target.title: feat(mac): Quick Chat — global-shortcut floating composer for the main session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sending a quick message to the main-session agent on macOS currently requires opening the full chat window (menu bar → Open Chat) or the dashboard. There is no fast, keyboard-first way to fire off a thought and get back to what you were doing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a **Quick Chat** bar to the macOS app: a Spotlight-style floating composer summoned by a configurable global shortcut (default ⌥Space) or the menu bar item.

- Shows who you're talking to: agent avatar (emoji or fallback symbol) + name fetched via `agent.identity.get`, with a "main session" chip so the routing is explicit.
- Return sends into the main session over the existing `chat.send` path (UUID idempotency key, reused verbatim on ambiguous transport retries so an admitted run is never duplicated). Command-Return sends and opens the full chat window; Shift-Return inserts a newline; Escape, clicking outside, resigning key, or re-pressing the shortcut dismisses.
- When notifications, accessibility, or screen recording are missing, an attached strip below the composer lists them with **Grant** / **Not now**. The bar deliberately avoids `PermissionMonitor` (its 1s poll executes an AppleScript probe against Terminal) and instead does a cheap targeted status poll of just those three capabilities while the bar is visible, so the strip clears live as permissions are granted. Dismissal is suppressed mid-grant so the TCC dialogs don't kill the bar.
- Non-activating key panel (`.nonactivatingPanel` + `canBecomeKey`) so typing works without activating the app — appears on the cursor's screen, top-third, with material background, shadow, and fade+rise animation in / fade-drop out. Panel height animates as the permission strip or multi-line text appears.
- Global shortcut via [KeyboardShortcuts](https://github.com/sindresorhus/KeyboardShortcuts) 3.0.1 (exact-pinned): Carbon-based, so no Input Monitoring/Accessibility permission is needed, and Settings → General gets a shortcut recorder row.
- Shared `ChatSendStatus` acceptance mapping extracted; `TalkModeRuntime` now uses it instead of private duplicates.
- The status-item-anchored compact panel was previously called "quick chat" in onboarding/docs copy; that wording now says "compact chat panel" and Quick Chat names this feature.

Follow-up (out of scope here): the same bar cross-platform via the Tauri app.

## User Impact

New opt-out-free feature: press ⌥Space (or record another chord in Settings → General, or use the menu bar item) to get a floating composer that sends to the main session. Replies land in the regular chat window. No new TCC permission surface; no config/schema changes; no gateway changes.

Release-note context: `feat(mac): Quick Chat — global-shortcut floating composer for the main session with agent identity and permission guidance`.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): prevent stale encrypted reasoning failures
target.body:
fix #95441

Related: #95493
Related: #95587

AI-assisted: yes (GitHub Copilot).

## What Problem This Solves

Persisted GitHub Copilot reasoning can become invalid when OpenClaw reconstructs a session, causing `invalid_encrypted_content` or a missing reply on a later turn. The rejection can happen while creating a Responses request or after its SSE stream opens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix uses the existing owner boundaries:

- **Cold replay history:** the GitHub Copilot provider's `sanitizeReplayHistory` hook removes persisted thinking/reasoning when a Copilot Responses `AgentSession` is rehydrated. The sanitized history becomes that session's in-memory state, while reasoning generated later in the same agent/tool loop remains available.
- **Active wire payload:** the provider boundary preserves complete native `rs_*` reasoning, converts Copilot connection-bound reasoning IDs to idless replay, keeps already-idless reasoning, and removes foreign, malformed, or incomplete reasoning. Existing message/function-call ID normalization remains intact.
- **Single bounded recovery:** Responses request creation and SSE draining share one retry budget. Before any public model output, a recognized encrypted-content failure retries once after removing only the top-level `encrypted_content` field from reasoning items. The retry preserves reasoning summaries and IDs, assistant messages, function calls, function outputs, and their order. Requests containing compaction fail closed instead of dropping compaction or constructing an item without its required ciphertext.

This separates prevention from recovery because neither is sufficient alone. Applying only a broad replay policy would discard valid same-loop continuity; relying only on recovery would keep sending known-stale state and make provider failure part of the normal path. Provider-owned cold sanitation plus one bounded generic fallback avoids both without adding session state, configuration, or a compatibility path.

The change adds no configuration, persisted replay state, transcript mutation, or public SDK surface.

## User Impact

Rehydrated Copilot sessions no longer send persisted opaque reasoning. Valid same-loop reasoning and tool continuation remain available. If a provider rejects stale reasoning before output starts, recovery preserves the continuation structure; compaction remains untouched and fails closed.

## Upstream Behavior References

- [`@github/copilot@1.0.69-2`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@github/copilot/v/1.0.69-2), build `546d22a58d`: active history retains encrypted reasoning, while cold resume, abort/cancel, and effective-model history rewrite strip opaque reasoning.
- [`github/copilot-sdk@5adb51b`](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/5adb51b9e2ac50ad4876e756fa8c05549c1490fd/nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts#L1044-L1054) documents OpenAI encrypted reasoning as session-bound and stripped on resume.
- [`microsoft/vscode@47657de`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L145-L172) requests `reasoning.encrypted_content`; its [history selection](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L306-L395) excludes pre-marker history, and its [serializer](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L631-L660) replays only complete Responses reasoning.
- OpenAI Node `6.45.0` models reasoning ciphertext as optional while compaction ciphertext is required; the recovery path therefore strips only reasoning ciphertext and never mutates compaction.
- #72602 records the live Copilot CAPI matrix: exact original or omitted reasoning IDs are accepted with original ciphertext; synthetic reasoning IDs are rejected.

## Evidence

- Current exact head: `243967371b74bc66113637dbc7ef099e45acaf69`; 8 files, `+729/-241` (970 changed lines, `size: L`).
- Builder-driven Responses continuation proof passed 57 tests, including create-time and streamed rejection, response-ID reset, one shared retry budget, abort/output-start guards, preservation of reasoning/message/function-call/function-output order, unchanged ID-only reasoning, and create/drain compaction no-retry.
- GitHub Copilot connection-bound-ID and stream-wrapper proof passed 15 tests. The focused cold-resume provider integration passed (1 test; 30 unrelated tests skipped).
- Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint passed for all 8 PR files; `git diff --check` passed.
- Full local tsgo/aggregate lint was blocked by this linked worktree's stale dependency install missing existing `@types/web-push`; no dependency files are changed. Exact-head GitHub CI is running for the current commit.
- The primary cold-resume behavior was previously credentialed-live-tested on the unchanged provider sanitation path: one visible reply, `invalid_encrypted_content = 0`, and `LLM request failed = 0`. The current retry-only follow-up has no local Copilot credential, so that reactive fallback remains an explicit live-proof gap.
- Current-main manual review found no remaining actionable issue after replacing the destructive retry. The prior P1 path that removed reasoning/compaction while retaining tool continuation no longer exists.
- The test-only size compression retained all 57 focused cases; a read-only review found no weakened assertion or shared-state regression.

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which is a poor fit for native approval or form-card flows.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. When a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw records the tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` runner path, ending the turn cleanly until a later inbound event resumes the session.

The implementation stays generic and channel-agnostic: channel plugins can opt in after their external side effect succeeds, while existing tools and plugins continue to behave the same when no `control` field is returned.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the eventual user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration.

target.title: fix: strip JSON5 trailing commas from YAML frontmatter before parsing (#108432)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace skills with JSON5-style trailing commas in flow-mapping metadata blocks inside SKILL.md frontmatter fail to parse as valid YAML 1.2 and are silently dropped from skill discovery with zero log output.

The YAML parser (yaml@2, schema: "core") rejects trailing commas in flow collections ({…} / […]), causing parseYamlFrontmatter to fall back to parseLineFrontmatter which cannot handle structured metadata values. The broken metadata leads to the skill being silently dropped by loadSingleSkillDirectory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Users who write frontmatter with trailing commas (a common JSON5 convention) lose their skill metadata silently with no error. The line-based fallback parser cannot retain structured values (arrays, objects), so metadata like tags: [ai, chat,] becomes an empty string.

## User Impact

- Before: frontmatter with trailing commas silently loses structured metadata → skill appears without tags, descriptions, or other metadata
- After: trailing commas are stripped before YAML parsing, preserving all metadata
- No regression: if the preprocessed block still fails to parse, the existing fallback to parseLineFrontmatter still applies

## Evidence

Live test verification: verified the stripJson5TrailingCommas regex against 8 edge cases (trailing commas in flow mapping, flow sequence, nested structures, middle commas preserved, strings with commas, empty content). 8/8 pass with zero false positives.

- Trailing comma in flow mapping:  →  ✅
- Trailing comma in flow sequence:  →  ✅
- Middle commas preserved:  unchanged ✅
- Strings with commas:  unchanged ✅
- Empty/whitespace: unchanged ✅

The preprocessor is safe by design: regex only removes commas followed by optional whitespace then  or . The YAML parse is wrapped in try/catch — a malformed preprocessed block never propagates an error.
